description:
The City of Flagler Beach owns and operates wastewater collection and conveyance infrastructure necessary to provide reliable wastewater service to residents, businesses, and visitors. Lift Station 4 (LS-04), located on North 20th Street, and Pump Station 8 (PS-08), located at 700 Moody Lane, have been identified for rehabilitation to address existing operational, mechanical, electrical, and structural needs.
The City issued Invitation to Bid No. FB-26-0109 for the Lift Station 4 and Pump Station 8 Rehabilitation Project. The project includes rehabilitation of the existing facilities, including pump replacement, electrical and control system improvements, bypass pumping, structural repairs, wet-well modifications, generator pads, piping improvements, and associated work necessary to return the facilities to proper operating condition.
The City received and evaluated bids submitted in response to the Invitation to Bid. The bid tabulation was reviewed by City staff and the Engineer for compliance with the Contract Documents and to determine the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.
The recommended award is in the amount of $545,785.95 for the completion of the Lift Station 4 and Pump Station 8 Rehabilitation Project.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach maintains multiple lift stations that are essential to the safe and reliable operation of the wastewater collection system. Routine inspections have identified structural deterioration, corrosion, and surface degradation within Lift Station 4 and Lift Station 8, requiring full rehabilitation and application of a protective monolithic lining system.
GML Coatings, LLC. submitted Proposal #26124, dated September 29, 2026, outlining a comprehensive rehabilitation process including sandblasting, 4000‑psi power washing, substrate resurfacing, leak‑stop application, primer installation, and final coating using the Green Monster™ Structural system. The proposal states:
“Surface preparation will begin by sandblasting the entire substrate… After sandblasting is completed, the surface area will be power washed at 4000psi…” “Green Monster™ Structural is spray applied at a 250 mil thickness… creating a 100% monolithic lining system throughout the structure.”The proposal includes detailed line‑item pricing for both lift stations:
Lift Station 4 Total: $29,613.58
Lift Station 8 Total: $35,265.58
Combined Project Cost: $64,879.16
The scope includes corrosion protection, patching and profiling, internal leak‑stop application, wet well cleaning, and mobilization. GML Coatings has demonstrated reliability and technical capability on similar projects throughout Florida, and the proposed work aligns with industry standards for structural rehabilitation of wastewater assets.
The proposal also notes:
“This proposal is based on GML Coatings work plans in an un‑obstructed area… Pricing is based upon award of complete scope with 1 mobilization…”Staff has reviewed the proposal and determined that the work is necessary to maintain system integrity, prevent further deterioration, and ensure long‑term operational reliability.
title: Resolution 2026‑89. A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, approving Proposal #26124 from GML Coatings, LLC. for rehabilitation and coating services at Lift Station 4 and Lift Station 8; approving a project budget of $64,879.16; providing funding, implementation, and an effective date.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach owns and operates a wastewater collection system and a 1.0 MGD wastewater treatment facility. The system has experienced sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs), regulatory compliance issues, and storm-related damage during Hurricane Milton. To address these challenges, the City initiated multiple lift station improvement projects and completed a Stormwater Master Plan.
Four critical facilities—LS-07, LS-08, PS-03, and PS-06—were identified for evaluation under the State Revolving Fund (SRF) program. McKim & Creed prepared the SAHM Lift Station & Stormwater Facilities Work Plan to assess alternatives and recommend improvements. Two alternatives and a "No Action" option were considered. Alternative 2, which rehabilitates LS-07, PS-03, and PS-06 in place and relocates LS-08, was selected as the recommended plan. This approach balances flood resiliency, operational reliability, and stormwater infrastructure improvements.
Proposed improvements include:
Replacement of mechanical components, pumps, and piping.
Structural, electrical, and control upgrades.
Improved access and flood protection measures.
Stormwater drainage enhancements (new piping, inlets, swales, grading, and roadway drainage).
The plan supports compliance with Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) requirements and provides a practical implementation strategy for long-term resiliency. Adoption of the Facility Plan is required to establish eligibility for SRF funding and to proceed with permitting, procurement, and construction.
title: Resolution 2026-83. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, relating to the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) State Revolving Fund (SRF), adoption of the Wastewater Facility Plan for the implementation of lift station improvements; providing for an effective date.

attachments.name: DDS Enterprises - Estimate 1252 for S. Flagler Avenue Demolition

description:
The City of Flagler Beach acquired the property located at 1336 S. Flagler Avenue following abandonment by the homeowner. The existing residential structure remaining on the property is in need of demolition and removal to eliminate potential safety concerns and facilitate future use of the site.
DDS Enterprises, LLC, submitted Estimate No. 1252, dated October 19, 2026, to perform demolition and disposal of the residence and associated materials for a total cost not to exceed $29,300.00. The proposal includes demolition and removal of the structure, roofing materials, trusses, windows, doors, furniture, bathroom fixtures, drywall, trim, flooring materials, concrete slab, block walls, driveway, sidewalk, disposal fees, silt fencing, grading, mobilization, and a contingency for permit fees if required.
The contractor's proposal specifies that utility disconnections will be handled separately and are not included within the contractor's scope of work. Existing trees, shrubs, and bushes will remain on site but may be subject to incidental damage during demolition activities. Upon completion, the site will be rough graded and cleared of dangerous debris. Staff has reviewed the proposal and determined that demolition of the abandoned structure is necessary and in the best interest of the City.
DDS Enterprises, LLC, is a vetted vendor who is included on the approved list of Qualified Vendors which was approved at the June 26, 2025, Commission Meeting.
The existing structure is in a state of disrepair. The combination of a damaged, open, and exposed roof, along with prior flooding that was never properly remediated, has resulted in conditions that render the structure uninhabitable. The structure was constructed in 1978, and was built below the current required Base Flood Elevation (BFE) and is in Flood Zone AE High-risk Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHA) per the FEMA FIRM Map. Staff is of the opinion that demolition and subsequent sale of the vacant lot would provide an opportunity for a new single-family residential building that complies with current flood protection requirements. Additionally, construction of a new residence would be subject to the City's stormwater review process, ensuring that the property is appropriately graded, and drainage requirements are addressed.
title: Resolution 2026-98. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, approving DDS Enterprises, LLC, to demolish the existing residential structure located at 1336 S. The conditions were:Upon installation of the upland buffer silt fence, the applicant to provide to the Building Department pre-construction, and post construction photos capturing the entire length of the perimeter silt fence corridor (photo field – wide angle beginning at the side and rear of the building structures.

Staff is currently working on getting that manhole and associated sanitary line transferred to the City of Flagler Beach.

Sec. 8.05.03. - Approval process
(b)Major site plan(9)A site plan shall not expire so long as a building permit remains active without interruption. However, if the owner abandons the site for a period of six (6) months, or the owner fails to perform any meaningful or significant work on the site for a period of six (6) months, or if the owner fails to achieve substantial performance of the work described in the building permit within two (2) years of the date of issuance, the site plan approval shall expire. Meaningful or significant work shall mean work performed in a workman like manner that is carried out in a manner that the obvious purpose and intent of the work is to complete the site within the customary period of time for the construction industry.
Attorney Smith advised staff that short of starting the entire Site Plan Approval Process, Section 8.05.03 (b)(11)(b) offers the approving entity (City Commission) could extend the validity of the original approval.

attachments.name: FIRST ADDENDUM TO INTERLOCAL AGREEMENT BETWEEN FLAGLER COUNTY AND THE CITY OF FLAGLER BEACH REGARDING DUNE RESTORATION PROJECTS
ILA for Beach Management, Flagler Beach and Flagler County

description:
The original ILA was entered into on October 08, 2019, to establish obligations for each entity related to the Dune Restoration Project (Reach I Project). The purpose of the 1st amendment is to establish the obligations for the Reach II Project.
The notable difference between the two documents is Section 2.3 which would require the City to pay the County $98,250 annually prior to October 15th. The agreement states the County would restrict the funds to be used for beach restoration and maintenance of Reach II within our city limits. The County advised they developed a cost estimate for the Reach II Project annual maintenance, then divided the cost proportionally between Flagler Beach, Beverly Beach and the County based upon linear feet. The second difference is "including leveling of "escarpments." The original ILA stated we would be responsible for "post-construction maintenance." In conversation with the City Manager, he stated that he conversed with Jason Harrah, ACOE, and Mr. Harrah advised that the leveling of the escarpments would be included in the required maintenance. This is not a new requirement.
title: Consider approving an Interlocal Agreement with Flagler County regarding beach maintenance.

attachments.name: Sign in Sheet - Pre-Proposal Meeting - RFQ FB26-0107 - Clearwell Tank Design

description:
The City of Flagler Beach continues to experience increasing demands on its public water system due to growth within its service area. The City's Water Treatment Plant (WTP), located at 4680 Seminole Woods Boulevard in Palm Coast, currently relies on a 0.085-million-gallon clearwell for finished water storage. Additional storage capacity consists of a 1.0-million-gallon ground storage tank and a 0.40-million-gallon elevated storage tank located on the barrier island. Existing storage limitations require significant operator intervention and reduce system resiliency during abnormal operating conditions or emergency events.
To address these concerns, the City previously evaluated alternatives for expanding storage and pumping capacity at the WTP. Following that evaluation, construction of a new 1.0-million-gallon in-ground clearwell and associated high-service pump station was identified as the preferred alternative for improving operational reliability, increasing redundancy, and supporting future system demands.
In July 2026, the City issued RFQ FB26-0107 for professional engineering services associated with the clearwell project. Through the competitive consultant selection process, McKim & Creed, Inc. was selected as the highest-ranked and most qualified firm to provide the required engineering and design services. Following negotiations, the consultant submitted a detailed scope of services and fee proposal for project management, data collection, field investigations, preliminary engineering, permitting coordination, and preparation of design documents through the 60% design phase.
The proposed scope includes:
Project management and coordination throughout the design effort.
Topographic and boundary surveying.
Subsurface utility engineering and utility conflict identification.
Geotechnical investigations.
Environmental and wetland evaluations.
Preliminary design and engineering analyses.
Development of a Preliminary Design Report.
Preparation of 60% design documents, technical specifications, and engineer's opinion of probable construction costs.
Coordination meetings with regulatory agencies and permitting authorities.
The proposed design will include a new 1.0-million-gallon cast-in-place concrete clearwell, a new high-service pump station, utility relocations, and associated electrical, instrumentation, and process improvements necessary to support reliable plant operations.
The consultant's proposed schedule anticipates completion of design support services within approximately eight weeks of Notice to Proceed, delivery of the Preliminary Design Report within twenty weeks, and completion of the 60% design package within thirty-two weeks.
Staff has reviewed the scope and fee proposal and finds the proposed work to be comprehensive, reasonable, and necessary to advance this critical infrastructure project toward construction. The proposed services will provide the engineering information needed to refine project costs, develop permit strategies, and position the City for future funding opportunities and construction implementation.
title: Resolution 2026‑62. A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, awarding professional engineering design services for a new 1‑million‑gallon (1MG) clearwell tank to McKim & Creed; approving a project budget of $521,903.70; providing funding, implementation, and an effective date.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach has identified issues with audio and video streaming during commission meetings, which persist despite troubleshooting efforts and replacement of cables and microphones. As such, replacement of the system is recommended and relocation of the equipment rack to prevent damage in the future. A contract with University of Central Florida was identified and reviewed with IM Solutions LLC, meeting the requirements to provide the service.
IM Solutions provided a demonstration onsite of their proposed solution over the summer. The improvements needed include microphones, speakers, cabling, POE switches, equipment rack and relocation, in-tile speakers, new mounting for video presentations, Dias monitors, processors, decoders & encoders, and a touch panel for sound.
City staff contacted the current provider, AVG Inc, for a quote but received no response.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach Public Works Department has initiated a swale rehabilitation project to restore drainage capacity within the area bounded by South 16th Street through South 22nd Street, including portions of South Central Avenue, South Daytona Avenue, and South Flagler Avenue. The project consists of re-establishing roadside swales in accordance with City Standard Detail "Swale Upgrades Driveway Details" to improve stormwater conveyance and reduce standing water along roadway shoulders.
The project area is shown below:
The rehabilitation effort includes excavation of roadside swales approximately nine inches deep, with side slopes not exceeding 4:1, followed by sod stabilization. Swales will be constructed where practical while maintaining existing driveway access and avoiding continuous excavation through intersections and certain developed areas.
The purpose of the project is to direct stormwater runoff into the roadside drainage system rather than allowing water to pond along roadway shoulders. Restoring positive drainage will improve stormwater management, increase infiltration, and provide additional temporary stormwater detention within existing rights-of-way.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach provides essential sewer and utility services to residents, businesses, and visitors, and maintaining reliable infrastructure is vital to public health and safety. As stated in the resolution, “the City currently lacks permanent bypass pumping equipment, relies on aging service vehicles, and has no internal sewer inspection crawler unit,” leaving critical systems vulnerable to failure and slowing disaster recovery.
The City previously submitted an application to the USDA Rural Development Community Facilities Disaster Assistance Program seeking funding for three bypass pumps, one service vehicle, and one sewer camera crawler unit. The original service vehicle cost was listed at $40,000. USDA has since requested that the City pursue a new vehicle rather than a used one, resulting in an updated cost of $59,320. This change increases the total project cost from $343,672 to $362,992.
Because the USDA requires the application to reflect accurate pricing, the City Commission must approve this amendment to the previously submitted grant application. As noted in the resolution, “the City Commission hereby authorizes staff to prepare and submit an application… and further authorizes the Mayor and City Manager to execute all documents necessary to complete the application process.”
title: Resolution 2026‑74. A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, authorizing an amendment to the application submitted to the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA Rural Development) Community Facilities Disaster Assistance Program to update the cost of the service vehicle and revise the total project budget to $362,992; providing funding, implementation, and an effective date.

attachments.name: Exhibit A 2026-78 Water Asset Managment Plan

description:
The City of Flagler Beach operates a drinking water system that provides essential water service to the community. The Florida Rural Water Association (FRWA), in partnership with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) State Revolving Fund (SRF) Program, prepared a Water System Asset Management and Fiscal Sustainability (AMFS) Plan for the City. The Plan evaluates the condition and criticality of the City's drinking water system assets and provides recommendations for long-term asset protection, maintenance, capital planning, funding, and utility financial sustainability.
The AMFS Plan identifies critical assets and processes requiring capital and/or operational funding, including failed or poor-condition hydrants and valves and a failed VFD at the booster station. It also establishes a Priority Action List addressing asset management, preventive maintenance, asset replacement, capital improvements, financial planning, and annual updates to the Plan. Among the identified priorities are replacement of failed hydrants and valves, replacement of VFD 3 at the booster station, AC pipe replacement, design and construction of Wells 17 and 18, continued work on the Lambert Street river crossing, and continued evaluation of system needs and funding opportunities.
Adoption of the AMFS Plan by Resolution is identified in the Plan as a required action for participation in the State Revolving Fund program. The Resolution authorizes the City Manager to implement the Plan and take actions necessary to pursue SRF funding. The Resolution also provides for annual evaluation of existing water rates and rate adjustments consistent with the financial recommendations of the AMFS Plan and the needs of the water system.
title: Resolution 2026-78. A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, approving the Water System Asset Management and Fiscal Sustainability Plan; authorizing the City Manager to take all actions necessary to effectuate the intent of this Resolution; and providing for an effective date.

description:
The Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic has been held in Flagler Beach for many years. Ordinance 2025-19 provides an overview of the special event process and procedures and the current Fee and Fine schedule outlines the cost of City resources should they be needed to support a special event. This year, the Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic will span three full days (past events were two days) and will require City resources such as police staffing, sanitation services, rental of barricades/cones to block off parking, and inspection of scaffolding. Since this is one of the biggest surf events of the year, and Saturday, October 24th, is expected to draw the largest crowd, Chief Blanchette supported the Tants in engaging Flagler Assist volunteers to help with A1A crossings at the event site and has added just one FB officer for security purposes on the 24th. Lastly, since the Tants provided the City with a Release of Liability, we will not need to bring in an off-duty lifeguard to cover the event on Friday, October 23rd. The City will have lifeguards on duty on the 24th and 25th as is typical during this time of the year, and we will not charge for this service.
The applicants are requesting a waiver of fees for the event. The Code of Ordinance Chapter 4, Article III Special Events Sec. 4-107. - Exemptions from special event requirements. (b) Any special event applicant may request a need-based application fee waiver from the city commission.
title: Consider a request for a waiver of fees for a Special Event Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Contest as regulated by Chapter 4, Article III Special Events Section 4-108(b). Applicant Will Tant.

Applicant: Redneck Rick Backyard Cooking – 1536 S. Ocean Shore Boulevard, Flagler Beach, Florida 32136. The subject property is zoned Tourist Commercial T.C. The applicant is seeking approval of an Annual Outdoor Entertainment Permit to allow amplified and non-amplified events consisting of music, spoken word and/or other forms of entertainment. The application indicates the entertainment will be on Fridays between the hours of 6:00 and 8:00 p.m. and Saturdays between the hours of 4:00 and 8:00 p.m.
Section 4-167, Review of Permit Application states, the City Commission, after receiving recommendation from the Planning and Architectural Review Board (PARB), shall approve, approve with conditions, or deny a permit for outdoor entertainment activity based on any of the following grounds:
(1) The activity would present an adverse impact on the health, safety or welfare of the applicant, participants, public employees or members of the public and/or fail to protect the city's environment.
(2) The activity would unreasonably inconvenience the general public.
(3) The proposed activity is prohibited by or inconsistent with the Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances or the Flagler Beach Comprehensive Plan.
(4) The applicant cannot meet, or is unwilling to meet, all the requirements of this article.
(5) The activity is proposed for a site that does not have adequate parking to accommodate the activity.
(6) The activity is proposed for a site that is inherently hazardous to the participants or the public.
(7) The event would have an adverse effect, and would unreasonably infringe upon, the rights of property owners within two hundred (200) feet of the property line of the subject property.
(8) The event would conflict with another proximate event or interfere with construction or maintenance work.
(9) The information furnished in the application is not materially complete and accurate.
(10) The applicant has violated a provision, restriction or condition of this article or an outdoor entertainment activity permit issued to the applicant within the past and has not presented competent substantial evidence that measures to prevent future violations will be implemented at the property.
(11) The requirements identified by the city staff to ensure public health, safety and welfare have not been met.
(12) The comments and/or recommendations of the planning and architectural review board have not been addressed.
(13) The proposed event or activity is prohibited by federal, state, or local regulations.
(14) Other issues in the public’s interest as identified by the city commission.
(a) In deciding to approve a permit the city commission may limit the type and number of temporary structures and the duration of the activity, including the hours and the number of days of the activity conducted to minimize any adverse impact caused by the activity.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach operates a drinking water system that provides essential water service to the community. The Florida Rural Water Association (FRWA), in partnership with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) State Revolving Fund (SRF) Program, prepared a Water System Asset Management and Fiscal Sustainability (AMFS) Plan for the City. The Plan evaluates the condition and criticality of the City's drinking water system assets and provides recommendations for long-term asset protection, maintenance, capital planning, funding, and utility financial sustainability.
The AMFS Plan identifies critical assets and processes requiring capital and/or operational funding, including failed or poor-condition hydrants and valves and a failed VFD at the booster station. It also establishes a Priority Action List addressing asset management, preventive maintenance, asset replacement, capital improvements, financial planning, and annual updates to the Plan. Among the identified priorities are replacement of failed hydrants and valves, replacement of VFD 3 at the booster station, AC pipe replacement, design and construction of Wells 17 and 18, continued work on the Lambert Street river crossing, and continued evaluation of system needs and funding opportunities.
title: Water System Asset Management and Fiscal Sustainability Plan

description:
The proposed FY27 Fee Schedule includes updates to the City’s fees to ensure that charges remain reflective of current costs, applicable regulations, and the services provided by the City. The proposed schedule incorporates several substantive updates, along with minor adjustments to existing fees.Key updates include:
Mobility Impact Fees: Addition of mobility impact fees to the City’s fee schedule to establish a mechanism for collecting the applicable costs associated with the transportation impacts of new development.
Building Permit Fees: Restructuring of the building permit fee schedule to comply with the requirements of House Bill 803 (HB 803). The revised structure updates the City’s building permit fees in accordance with the legislation and provides a more consistent and transparent fee schedule.
Sanitation Fees: Minor adjustments to select sanitation-related fees to reflect updated service costs and maintain the appropriate level of cost recovery.
Other Fee Updates: Additional minor revisions and administrative updates have been incorporated throughout the schedule to improve clarity, consistency, and accuracy.
If approved by the City Commission at the September 24, 2026 Commission meeting, the updated FY27 Fee Schedule will become effective October 1, 2026, in conjunction with the start of the new fiscal year.
Overall, the FY27 Fee Schedule is intended to provide a clear and current framework for City fees while supporting appropriate cost recovery, complying with legislative requirements, and ensuring that fees remain aligned with the services and regulatory activities they support.

description:
Most notably through the efforts of Dr. Lee Richards, the City of Flagler Beach has been awarded federal funding through the Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) Program, administered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and passed through the Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM). The award supports the elevation of four residential structures that have experienced repetitive flooding and are vulnerable to future flood events.
The State of Florida, through FDEM, has issued Contract B0313 for Project FMA‑PJ‑04‑FL‑2023‑005, titled City of Flagler Beach Elevations. The agreement provides $914,423.40 in federal funds to support design, permitting, elevation construction, compliance documentation, and close‑out activities.
“Amount of Federal Funds Obligated by this Agreement: $914,423.40.” — Federally‑Funded Subaward and Grant Agreement, Award Table
The project includes the elevation of four houses located at:
2408 S Daytona Avenue
910 S Flagler Avenue
918 S Flagler Avenue
308 S 25th Street
Each structure must be elevated at least two feet above Base Flood Elevation, consistent with NFIP, ASCE 24‑14, and Florida Building Code requirements.
The Agreement designates Justin Isaacs, Administrative Assistant to the City Engineer, as the City’s authorized representative responsible for administration, reporting, coordination, and compliance.
The period of performance begins upon execution and ends April 26, 2029.

A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, authorizing execution of the Federally‑Funded Subaward and Grant Agreement (Contract B0313) with the Florida Division of Emergency Management for Flood Mitigation Assistance Project FMA‑PJ‑04‑FL‑2023‑005; approving acceptance of $914,423.40 in federal funding; providing for administration, implementation, and an effective date.

description:
The City Commission had previously adopted the following Vision Statement:
Flagler Beach is a diverse coastal community committed to enhancing our quality of life by:
Preserving our environment as a community asset.
Maintaining our old Florida heritage and small-town charm.
Providing a safe, healthy, and clean environment.
Supporting the development of local business to provide services to residents.
Promoting and supporting eco-tourism through our natural resources.
Providing opportunities for education, culture, and recreation.
The City Commission subsequently developed a series of Strategic Priorities Leading to 2032 (April 26, 2022) and Goals for Implementing the Strategic Priorities (April 26, 2022). A summary of the April 26, 2022 efforts is attached.
At its April 1, 2026 Strategic Visioning Session, the City Commission reviewed and discussed the 2022 documents, recognizing that some goals had been completed, others no longer appropriate, others necessitating revision, and others still in need of pursuit. A summary of the results of the April 1 review and discussion is attached.
The final attachment is the proposed revisions, based upon the April 1, 2026 discussions, to the City Vision Statement, the Strategies Leading to 2032, and the Goals for Implementing the Strategic Priorities.
The series of all three documents was presented to the City Commission at its August 27, 2026 Regular Meeting. No subsequent comments have been received; therefore, Resolution 2026-77 adopts the proposed revisions.

description:
Chief Quartier requested to surplus the equipment from inventory for the following reasons.
Engine 12
VIN: 4P1CT02A44A004229
Year: 2004
Make: Pierce
Model: Enforcer
Recommended Disposal Method: Public Auction / Surplus Sale
E-12 was purchased in early 2024 for use as a reserve apparatus. The unit is over 20 years old and has been out of service since early 2026 due to a fire pump issue requiring repair. Due to its age, mechanical condition, and outdated apparatus design and safety features compared with current standards, continued investment in repairs and maintenance is not considered cost-effective.
The department currently operates a frontline pumper and frontline ladder truck, and the limited operational need for an additional aging reserve apparatus does not justify the ongoing costs associated with repair, maintenance, insurance, etc. It is recommended that E-12 be declared surplus and disposed of through public auction or other approved surplus property process.
Parts Engine
VIN: 4P1CE01A54A004249
Year: 2004
Make: Pierce
Model: Enforcer
Recommended Disposal Method: Scrap / Salvage
This apparatus was purchased in early 2024 for use as a source of replacement parts for E-12. The vehicle is not maintained as an operational apparatus and has remained unused and stored outdoors. Its continued deterioration reduces its value as a future source of usable components and creates an ongoing storage and property-management burden.
With the recommended disposal of E-12, there is no longer an operational need to retain a second 2004 apparatus solely for parts. Due to its age, condition, limited resale value as a complete operational apparatus, and lack of anticipated departmental use, it is recommended that the vehicle be declared surplus and disposed of for scrap, salvage, or parts in accordance with the City's surplus property procedures.
title: Resolution 2026-82. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, declaring certain property as surplus; providing for conflict and an effective date hereof.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach has long contemplated a parking management program (i.e., paid parking). Earlier this year, City staff solicited qualifications from interested vendors. Eight vendors submitted qualifications and an Evaluation Team selected four of the vendors to introduce themselves to the City Commission.
On August 11, the City Commission conducted a Parking Management Workshop and reviewed presentations from:
One Parking
Peninsula Partners Parking
LAZ Parking
Passport Parking
As indicated in the original Request for Qualifications, the City Commission should rank the four vendors listed above in order of preference to begin discussions for paid parking implementation and operations with the highest ranked vendor. If discussions are not fruitful, the City Commission will be notified and authorization sought to begin discussions with the second-ranked vendor (and continuing in a likewise fashion, if necessary).
The intent of the discussions is to develop an initial baseline of implementation and operations. Once developed, those preliminary factors will be presented to the City Commission for review and revision. This process will continue for as long as necessary to fully develop an implementation and operation plan or until the City Commission desires an alternative course of action. This effort will also incorporate comments and feedback from the Community Redevelopment Agency Advisory Board (and any other agencies or stakeholders as directed by the City Commission).

description:
Background: The employee health, dental and life insurance coverages are due for renewal 10/1/2026. The City currently utilizes United Healthcare for 3 plan options, Guardian for dental coverage and Florida Blue Cross Blue Shield for life insurance.
Medical: Through the City’s employee benefit consultant, Brown and Brown, United Healthcare proposed a renewal at a 34% increase. A market analysis was conducted and proposals were obtained from Florida Health Care, Florida Blue, United Healthcare, Curative, and Sidecar, with Florida Health Care and Sidecar providing the most competitive proposals. Sidecar has also offered a $20,000 implementation credit and a second-year rate cap of a 12% increase.
Dental: The City currently utilizes Guardian as our dental coverage provider. Dental insurance is primarily an employee paid benefit with a small City contribution. The City’s benefit consultant, Brown and Brown, conducted a market analysis for employee dental insurance and received proposals from Guardian, MetLife, United Healthcare and Sun Life. Guardian proposed a 40% premium increase. description:
The City of Flagler Beach maintains a critical network of fire hydrants to ensure adequate fire protection and public safety. A hydrant requiring replacement was identified. However, field-testing conducted jointly by City staff and the contractor determined that the hydrant cannot be isolated using existing infrastructure. Without corrective measures, replacement would require shutting off water service to the entire barrier island.
To address this issue, Gravity Services, Inc. has proposed installation of an 8‑inch line stop valve on South Daytona Avenue, allowing isolation of the hydrant with only a momentary interruption of service. In addition, Gravity Services has submitted a proposal for the overnight installation of a 6‑inch valve and hydrant replacement, including asphalt patching and flowable fill beneath the sidewalk to preserve existing infrastructure.
The City distributed the revised scope to other contractors. All other firms were either non‑responsive or submitted pricing that was unreasonably low and not reflective of the required work. Gravity Services, Inc. has demonstrated reliability, responsiveness, and accurate pricing on prior City projects, and is the only contractor providing a complete, feasible, and technically appropriate solution.
The deliverables under this project include installation of the 8‑inch line stop valve, replacement of the hydrant and associated 6‑inch valve, completion of all required restoration work such as asphalt patching and sidewalk preservation, and compliance testing and sampling following hydrant replacement. Work will be scheduled overnight to minimize service disruption. The outcome will be a fully functional hydrant with proper isolation capability, ensuring long‑term system reliability and fire protection capacity.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach operates a network of wastewater lift stations that provide essential conveyance of sewage to downstream treatment facilities. Three stations, Lift Station 1, Lift Station 7, and Lift Station 8, have been identified by staff as requiring rehabilitation to maintain reliable operation, reduce the risk of failure, and extend the useful life of critical infrastructure.
The locations of the stations are:Lift Station 1 – 246 Ocean Palm Drive
Lift Station 7 – 17 Oak Lane
Lift Station 8 – 1727 Windsong Circle
These stations exhibit aging mechanical and electrical components, deteriorated wet well coatings, and site conditions that require modernization to meet current operational and resiliency standards. Rehabilitation is necessary to ensure uninterrupted wastewater collection service and to reduce the likelihood of emergency failures that could impact residents and businesses.
Mead & Hunt, Inc., submitted a proposal, offering engineering services to support the rehabilitation of all three stations. Their scope includes project management, field data collection, pump testing, design development, preparation of construction documents, and bidding assistance.
Staff have reviewed the proposal and determined that the scope, schedule, and fee are appropriate and consistent with the City’s needs for this project.
Why This Work Is NeededAging Infrastructure: Mechanical and electrical components at all three stations have reached the end of their useful life and require replacement to maintain reliability.
Operational Reliability: Rehabilitation will reduce the risk of pump failures, electrical malfunctions, and wet well deterioration that could disrupt wastewater service.
Resiliency Improvements: The project includes floodproofing measures and site upgrades that enhance the City’s ability to maintain service during storm events.
Regulatory and Safety Considerations: Modernized equipment and improved site conditions support compliance with operational standards and reduce safety risks for staff.
Cost Avoidance: Proactive rehabilitation prevents more costly emergency repairs and mitigates the risk of environmental impacts.

Station Pump Test Findings

75% Design Review Meeting Summary
100% Design Drawings

description:
The City of Flagler Beach provides essential sewer and utility services to residents, businesses, and visitors. Repeated impacts from hurricanes — including Ian (2022), Nicole (2022), Idalia (2023), Debby (2024), Milton (2024), and Helene (2025) — have strained the City’s sewer systems, damaged lift stations, and highlighted vulnerabilities in emergency response capacity.
Currently, the City lacks permanent bypass pumping equipment, relies on aging service vehicles, and has no internal sewer inspection crawler unit. These gaps leave infrastructure vulnerable to undetected failures, delay recovery after disasters, and increase reliance on contractors and rentals that may not be available during regional emergencies.
Approval of this resolution is necessary to authorize staff to apply for USDA funding.
Hurricanes have repeatedly overwhelmed Flagler Beach’s sewer infrastructure, causing spills, lift station damage, and delayed recovery.
Reliance on rented bypass pumps and outside contractors has proven unsustainable during regional disasters.
Without modern service vehicles and diagnostic equipment, crews cannot respond quickly or inspect underground lines after storms.
Permanent equipment will allow the City to safeguard public health, maintain uninterrupted sewer service, and strengthen resilience against future disasters.
If awarded, the USDA grant will fund the acquisition of five critical pieces of equipment:
Three By‑Pass Pumps on Trailers — Provides immediate emergency pumping capacity during sewer line failures and flooding.
Service Truck Replacement — Ensures safe, reliable transportation for utility crews during daily operations and storm response. USDA has instructed the city to apply for the vehicle separately and to also not to include the quote for the service vehicle due to a blanket cost approval. That vehicle will be a separate grant application in the future.
Sewer Camera Crawler Unit — Gives the City its first in‑house capability to inspect sewer lines internally, reducing reliance on contractors and enabling proactive maintenance.
Together, these deliverables will directly benefit the City’s 5,200 residents and 2,600 households, ensuring reliable sewer service, rapid emergency response, and long‑term disaster resilience.

attachments.name: Sunset Cove FH Inserta Valve Change Order

description:
On July 28, 2026, U.S. Water was mobilized to perform a scheduled hydrant replacement at the municipal hydrant located at 300 Lambert Avenue. Following standard procedure, crews initiated excavation of the job site to expose the existing infrastructure. Once excavation was complete, personnel proceeded to shut down the water supply in preparation for removal and replacement of the hydrant assembly.
During the course of this operation, crews identified an unforeseen condition within the distribution system. Specifically, the 16‑inch transmission main was discovered to be back feeding into the 6‑inch distribution line serving the hydrant. This hydraulic interaction rendered isolation of the hydrant unfeasible under the current configuration, thereby preventing completion of the replacement as originally planned.
In order to address this complication and ensure reliable isolation of the hydrant for both immediate replacement and future maintenance activities, U.S. Water has proposed the installation of an “Inserta Valve.” This specialized valve assembly would be installed in-line to provide a dedicated shutoff mechanism, thereby allowing the hydrant to be isolated from the back feeding transmission main. Implementation of this solution will enable crews to safely terminate water flow to the hydrant, complete the replacement, and establish a more resilient service configuration moving forward.
DeliverablesThe contractor’s scope of work will include the following key deliverables:
Valve Installation: Furnish and install an Inserta Valve at the designated location to provide a dedicated isolation point for the hydrant.
Hydrant Replacement: Complete removal of the existing hydrant and installation of a new hydrant assembly once isolation is achieved.
System Integration: Ensure proper integration of the valve into the existing distribution system, with testing to confirm full operability.
Service Continuity: Implement measures to minimize water service disruption to adjacent customers during installation and replacement activities.
Documentation: Provide as‑built drawings, valve specifications, and a completion report detailing the corrective action taken and confirming hydrant operability.
Future Maintenance Capability: Deliver a configuration that allows the hydrant to be isolated independently for any subsequent service needs.
title: Resolution 2026‑66. A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, approving Change Order #2 with U.S. Water Services Corporation for hydrant work at Sunset Cove; approving a project budget of $34,304.92, subject to credit adjustments; providing funding, implementation, and an effective date.

attachments.name: Add WM River Crossing Subaqueous Portion Scope

description:
The City of Flagler Beach currently relies on a single water transmission main crossing the Intracoastal Waterway at North 3rd Street. This configuration presents a significant operational vulnerability: any failure, emergency repair, or unplanned outage at the crossing would disrupt potable water service and fire protection capacity for the barrier island. To address this risk, the City has planned construction of a redundant water main crossing at North 10th Street.
The upland portion of the redundant main along Lambert Avenue has already been designed, and construction bids have been received. The next step is to begin design of the subaqueous portion, which includes a trenchless river crossing and extension of the main eastward to SR A1A to connect to the existing transmission system.
Mead & Hunt, Inc. has submitted a Phase 1 design scope that includes project management, survey, geotechnical investigation, utility coordination, site reconnaissance, and preparation of 60% design documents. These tasks represent the foundational engineering work required before final design, permitting, and construction can proceed.
Why This Work Is NecessaryRedundancy: A second river crossing eliminates the City’s dependence on a single transmission line, reducing the risk of widespread service interruption.
Fire Protection: Maintaining uninterrupted water pressure is essential for hydrant performance and emergency response.
Operational Flexibility: A redundant crossing allows future maintenance or repairs without island‑wide shutdowns.
Infrastructure Resilience: The project aligns with long‑term system hardening and coastal resilience objectives.
Project Continuity: With the upland portion ready for award, initiating Phase 1 of the subaqueous design ensures the overall project remains on schedule for future construction.

description:
Ordinance 2026-15 passed First Reading on July 23, 2026. The Ordinance has been advertised as required by Section 166.041(3)(a) of the Florida Statutes. Line 83 of the Ordinance has been amended per the direction included in the motion to approve. The Section now reads: 2. Each violation may result in the issuance of a Notice of Violation and enforcement action as authorized under the City Code, including administrative penalties or suspension of sewer service if necessary to protect the city infrastructure.
The City of Flagler Beach owns and operates a publicly-owned treatment works (POTW) that collects and treats wastewater from residential, commercial, and industrial sources. Accumulation of fats, oils, and grease (FOG) within the wastewater collection system contributes to blockages, backups, sanitary sewer overflows, and increased maintenance costs.
To address these issues, staff has prepared a comprehensive Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) Program Manual, which establishes technical standards for grease interceptors and oil/water separators, including design, sizing, installation, cleaning, maintenance, recordkeeping, and inspection procedures. The Manual also includes a standardized FOG Maintenance Log for use by food service establishments.
Ordinance 2026‑15 formally creates the City’s FOG Management Program within the Code of Ordinances and authorizes the use of the FOG Program Manual as the governing technical document. Adoption of the ordinance and manual will improve system reliability, reduce maintenance burdens, and support compliance with State and Federal environmental requirements.
title: Ordinance 2026‑15 – An Ordinance of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, amending the Code of Ordinances to establish a Fats, Oils, and Grease (FOG) Management Program; providing for regulations governing the installation, maintenance, and inspection of grease interceptors and oil/water separators; providing for administrative procedures, enforcement; providing for severability; providing for codification; and providing for an effective date (Second [Final] Reading).

description:
Flagler County is amending the Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) cost sharing methodology. For many years, CAD fees have been allocated based on each agency’s percentage of personnel using the system. While this method has served Flagler County agencies, it does not fully reflect how public safety resources are actually utilized. To improve fairness, transparency, and accuracy, Flagler County will transition to a "call for service–based model," using data drawn directly from our E911 call logs. This approach aligns costs with real operational demand and ensures municipalities contribute proportionately to the services they utilize.
To help ensure a smooth transition for everyone involved, Flagler County has decided to phase in this change: Flagler County will absorb 60% of the allocated costs during the first year (FY27). This gives other agencies additional time to adjust budget plans and prepare for the full allocation, which will begin in FY28. See the FY27 fees below.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach operates and maintains 28 wastewater lift stations throughout the community. The N. 20th Street Lift Station has been identified by staff as requiring full rehabilitation due to aging mechanical components, deteriorated piping, outdated electrical systems, and structural deficiencies within the wet well. These conditions increase the risk of operational failure, sanitary sewer overflows, and regulatory non‑compliance.
Environmental Control Systems, Inc. (ECS), a qualified local contractor, submitted a detailed proposal dated June 2, 2026, outlining a comprehensive rehabilitation of the lift station. The proposal includes complete demolition of existing components, installation of new mechanical and electrical systems, bypass pumping, structural improvements, and all necessary labor, materials, and equipment.
The ECS proposal provides a turn-key rehabilitation package that restores the lift station to reliable operating condition and extends its service life. Staff has reviewed the proposal and determined that the scope of work is necessary and appropriate to ensure continued wastewater service reliability.
The N. 20th Street Lift Station is a critical component of the City’s wastewater collection system.
Existing components are deteriorated and at risk of failure, which could result in:Sanitary sewer overflows
Environmental impacts
Regulatory violations
Emergency repair costs
The proposed rehabilitation:Replaces all major mechanical and electrical components
Improves operational reliability and safety
Reduces long‑term maintenance costs
Ensures compliance with current electrical and safety standards
Extends the useful life of the lift station
ECS is a qualified local contractor with experience performing similar work for the City.
title: Resolution 2026‑51. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, approving a proposal from Environmental Control Systems, Inc. (ECS) for rehabilitation work at the N. 20th Street Lift Station (LS-04), authorizing a project budget in the amount of $295,500.00; providing for funding, implementation, conflict and an effective date. ​

description:
Pump Station 8 (located at Moody Lane and Lantana Avenue) is a critical component of the City’s wastewater collection system and requires full rehabilitation to maintain operational reliability, protect public health, and ensure compliance with applicable standards. The station’s existing valving, piping, electrical components, and pump assemblies have reached the end of their useful life and must be replaced to prevent service interruptions and potential environmental impacts.
City staff solicited proposals from qualified contractors for the complete rehabilitation of Pump Station 8. The scope includes:
Full bypass operations for up to 30 days
Demolition of existing components
Installation of new HDPE and ductile iron piping
New above‑ground valving assembly
New duplex pump package and rail system
Electrical rack, control panel, alert system, and conduit upgrades
Concrete cutting, core drilling, and wet well modifications
Confined space safety measures and site protection
Environmental Control Systems, Inc. (Flagler Septic) submitted a comprehensive proposal dated June 24, 2026, totaling $291,000.00. The proposal includes all labor, materials, bypass equipment, demolition, reconstruction, electrical work, pump package installation, concrete modifications, and safety requirements necessary to complete the project in accordance with City standards.
RCM Utilities, LLC submitted an estimate dated June 10, 2026, totaling $169,938.00. However, staff determined that RCM Utilities has been non‑responsive to multiple attempts to obtain clarifications.
The submitted quote omits several essential scope items, including:Line stop installation
Concrete restoration
Level controls
Pump‑off connection
Site restoration beyond basic backfill
The omissions indicate that the proposal does not reflect the full and correct scope of work required for Pump Station 8.
Based on responsiveness, completeness of scope, and alignment with City standards, staff recommends acceptance of the Environmental Control Systems, Inc. proposal.
title: Resolution 2026-57. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, accepting the proposal from Environmental Control Systems, Inc. for the rehabilitation of Pump Station 8; approving a project budget in the amount of $291,000.00; providing for funding, implementation, conflict, and an effective date.

description:

During the discussion and public hearings to adopt Ordinance 2025-28 approving the sale of the property known as Ocean Palm Golf Course, deed restrictions were agreed upon. The deed restrictions limit the use of the property to a golf course, golf clubhouse, clubhouse restaurant, and related golf recreational uses and events that are consistent with uses common for a golf course and golf clubhouse.
The deed restriction is only terminable by a unanimous vote of the City Commission. Concerns arose that an ordinance could be adopted that would amend the deed restriction from a unanimous vote to a majority vote. A Charter amendment was proposed to further secure the use of the property. Presented is an Ordinance approving a referenda item to amend the Charter to include the requirement for a unanimous vote of the Commission to amend the deed restriction, i.e.: the use of the property. The referenda item, if approved by the voters at the November 03, 2026, General Election, can not be changed unless approved by the electors.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach owns and operates a publicly owned treatment works (POTW) that collects and treats wastewater from residential, commercial, and industrial sources. Accumulation of fats, oils, and grease (FOG) within the wastewater collection system contributes to blockages, backups, sanitary sewer overflows, and increased maintenance costs.
To address these issues, staff has prepared a comprehensive Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) Program Manual, which establishes technical standards for grease interceptors and oil/water separators, including design, sizing, installation, cleaning, maintenance, recordkeeping, and inspection procedures. The Manual also includes a standardized FOG Maintenance Log for use by food service establishments.
Ordinance 2026‑15 formally creates the City’s FOG Management Program within the Code of Ordinances and authorizes the use of the FOG Program Manual as the governing technical document. Adoption of the ordinance and manual will improve system reliability, reduce maintenance burdens, and support compliance with State and Federal environmental requirements.
title: Ordinance 2026‑15 – An Ordinance of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, amending the Code of Ordinances to establish a Fats, Oils, and Grease (FOG) Management Program; providing for regulations governing the installation, maintenance, and inspection of grease interceptors and oil/water separators; providing for administrative procedures, enforcement; providing for severability; providing for codification; and providing for an effective date (First Reading).

description:
The City of Flagler Beach is advancing the Additional Water Main River Crossing project to improve potable water system redundancy, enhance operational reliability, and support long‑term utility capacity. The upland/Lambert Avenue portion includes installation of a new 16‑inch transmission main, valves, hydrants, tie‑ins, water services, and restoration.
Invitation to Bid No. FB‑2026‑0705 was publicly advertised, and sealed bids were received in accordance with Florida Statutes and City procurement requirements. 4C’s Trucking & Excavation, Inc. submitted the lowest responsive and responsible bid.
The Base Bid submitted by 4C’s totals $1,042,776.04, which includes the following major components:
16" PVC Water Main (2,800 LF @ $108.27/LF) – $303,156.00
Fire Hydrant Assemblies (7 EA @ $11,552.74/EA) – $80,869.18
Short‑Side and Long‑Side Water Services – $185,623.50 combined
Concrete, paver, and asphalt restoration – $96,302.35 combined
Sewer lateral adjustments/repairs required by Addendum No. 1
In addition to the Base Bid, staff recommends awarding the Additive Alternate, which totals $379,127.86. The alternate includes drainage improvements, culvert replacements, mitered end sections, swale regrading, and additional restoration work. Completing this work concurrently with the water main installation avoids future conflicts, reduces long‑term maintenance costs, and minimizes disruption to residents.
The combined award amount for the Base Bid and Additive Alternate is $1,421,903.90.
Mead & Hunt has reviewed the bid and recommends awarding both the Base Bid and Additive Alternate to 4C’s Trucking & Excavation, Inc.
1. System RedundancyThe City currently relies heavily on a single transmission route. A second river crossing and upland connection:
Reduces vulnerability to single‑point failures
Ensures continuous service during emergencies, repairs, or storm events
Strengthens the City’s overall water distribution resilience
2. Fire Protection ImprovementsThe project includes:
Seven new hydrants
Larger diameter main
Improved flow and pressure
This directly enhances fire suppression capability for residents and businesses.
3. Replacement of Aging InfrastructureExisting water main segments and appurtenances along Lambert Avenue are aging and undersized. This project:
Replaces outdated materials
Eliminates known weak points
Reduces future maintenance costs and emergency repairs
4. Required for the River Crossing ProjectThe upland portion is not optional — it is the mainland connection point for the new river crossing. Without this segment:
The river crossing cannot be placed into service
The City cannot achieve the intended redundancy
The project would remain incomplete
5. Regulatory and Operational BenefitsThe project supports:
Compliance with water system reliability standards
Improved operational flexibility
Better isolation and maintenance capability through new valves and line stops
6. Public Safety and Community ResilienceUltimately, the project protects:
Residents
Businesses
Visitors
Critical facilities
by ensuring the City can maintain water service and fire protection even during outages, storms, or infrastructure failures.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach maintains a network of fire hydrants that provides essential fire protection and public safety throughout the community. As part of ongoing system inspections and hydrant replacement planning, staff identified two locations, 300 Lambert Avenue and the corner of Sunset Cove and South Central Avenue, where hydrant replacement cannot be safely or effectively completed without additional corrective work.
300 Lambert Avenue – Need for Isolation Valve InstallationThe existing hydrant at this location cannot be replaced because the water line serving it does not contain an isolation valve. Without a valve, the City cannot safely shut down the line to remove and replace the hydrant.
Why this work is needed:
Ensures the hydrant can be isolated without affecting a larger portion of the distribution system.
Allows safe depressurization and replacement of the hydrant.
Brings the assembly into compliance with modern utility standards.
Deliverables:
Installation of a new 6‑inch isolation valve.
Installation of a new restraint.
Controlled shutdown and restoration of service.
Post‑replacement sampling and bacteriological testing.
Corner of Sunset Cove & South Central Avenue – Valve Failure and Unrestrained Tee ReplacementAt this location, the existing valve does not fully close, preventing proper isolation of the hydrant. Additionally, the tee serving the hydrant is an older, unrestrained push‑on fitting. This type of fitting is not designed to withstand the forces associated with shutdowns, depressurization, or hydrant replacement.
Why this work is needed:
Prevents potential failure of the unrestrained tee during hydrant replacement.
Ensures the line can be fully isolated for safe work.
Replaces aging components with modern, restrained mechanical‑joint fittings.
Deliverables:
Replacement of the existing push‑on tee with a restrained mechanical‑joint tee.
Installation of two mechanical‑joint sleeves.
Installation of a new 6‑inch isolation valve and restraint.
Controlled shutdown and restoration of service.
Post‑replacement sampling and bacteriological testing.
Operational RequirementsBoth locations require pre‑planned shutdowns on separate days to minimize service impacts and ensure proper sequencing. U.S. Water Services Corporation will perform all sampling and compliance testing following hydrant replacement.
title: Resolution 2026‑47. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach authorizing change‑order work with U.S. Water Services Corporation for fire hydrant repairs at 300 Lambert Avenue and the corner of Sunset Cove and South Central Avenue, in an amount not to exceed $10,217.89; providing for conflict and an effective date.

description:
In 2022/2023, the City federal utilized American Rescue Plan Act funds to construct a fiber optic network linking several City facilities. The connection of the facilities required boring under the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway and installing three conduits. The fiber optic network subsequently installed makes use of one of the three conduits. Representatives from MetroNet approached the City to lease one of the two remaining conduits to provide alternative fiber optic telecommunication services to beachside residents and businesses.
City staff consulted with Mr. Michael Tammaro to assist with determining an appropriate lease fee. Mr. Tammaro previously assisted the City in recommending the cable landing fee for DC Blox. Mr. Tammaro referenced the fee (per linear foot) charged by the Florida East Coast Railroad for boring under railroad tracks. FEC charges $8.00 per foot for such boring and the proposed agreement charges the same. MetroNet will utilize 600 feet of the conduit (the distance between the two access points to the conduit). The proposed agreement provides for an initial fee of $5,000 with a 5% annual escalator clause. MetroNet officials have further indicated that MetroNet will provide the connection to the planned City camera system at no charge, which will provide for secure connections (the original camera proposal was wireless-based) and should result in considerable savings (the monthly service fee for those connections has yet to be determined).
The City Attorney has prepared and reviewed the proposed agreement with MetroNet.
title: Consideration of Conduit License Agreement Between the City of Flagler Beach and Metro FiberNet, LLC.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach does not currently have reclaimed water production infrastructure at the wastewater treatment facility nor a distribution system network for public access reuse. All treated effluent from the facility is discharged into the Intracoastal Waterway (ICW) because no alternative effluent disposal systems exist.
In June 2021, the State of Florida enacted Senate Bill 64, requiring utilities statewide to eliminate surface water discharges, including discharges to the ICW, by January 1, 2032. To comply, the City must implement significant treatment facility upgrades, reclaimed water production systems, and distribution infrastructure.
The DEP grant opportunity totaling $43,166,645 will support these improvements. The project is structured using a phased approach consisting of seven distinct subprojects, as described below:
Phase 1: Design
Phase 2: Improvements to the existing wastewater treatment facility to upgrade the facility and replace obsolete equipment, including:
Reverse Osmosis (RO) treatment and concentrate disposal systems
Transfer Pump Station (TPS)
Covered 2‑MG reclaimed water ground storage tank
Reclaimed Water Distribution Pump Station (RWDPS)
Reclaimed water mains from the RWDPS to the periphery of the treatment facility for conveyance into the future reclaimed water distribution system
Phase 3: Distribution along John Anderson Highway West and South
Phase 4: Distribution along Roberts Road North
Phase 5: Distribution along Lambert Avenue / Palm Drive East and North
Phase 6: Distribution along Barrier Island Parks East
Phase 7: Distribution to Flagler Beach Golf Course South and East
This multi‑phase program will satisfy all SB 64 requirements and establish a complete reclaimed water production and distribution system for the City.
This initial request is for FY 2026–27 only. Grant requests 1 and 2 amounting to $13,498,500. Additional future grant proposals will be available for the remaining components of the reclaim water system.
title: Resolution 2026-55. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach authorizing City staff to pursue Florida Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) grant funding for reclaimed water system improvements totaling $43,166,645, to be implemented in six phases with a fifty‑fifty (50/50) cost share; providing for conflict and an effective date.

description:
During the discussion and public hearings to adopt Ordinance 2025-28 approving the sale of the property known as Ocean Palm Golf Course, deed restrictions were agreed upon. The deed restrictions limit the use of the property to a golf course, golf clubhouse, clubhouse restaurant, and related golf recreational uses and events that are consistent with uses common for a golf course and golf clubhouse.
The deed restriction is only terminable by a unanimous vote of the City Commission. Concerns arose that an ordinance could be adopted that would amend the deed restriction from a unanimous vote to a majority vote. A Charter amendment was proposed to further secure the use of the property. Presented is an Ordinance approving a referenda item to amend the Charter to include the requirement for a unanimous vote of the Commission to amend the deed restriction, i.e.: the use of the property. The referenda item, if approved by the voters at the November 03, 2026, General Election, can not be changed unless approved by the electors.
To qualify as a referenda item on the November 03, 2026, General Election Ballot, this Ordinance must be adopted and delivered to the Flagler County Supervisor of Elections before the deadline of August 07, 2026.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach is in the process of constructing a new Watewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) facility to support long‑term utility and operational needs. During project planning and site layout, it was determined that an existing Florida Power & Light (FPL) utility pole located at 2000 Avenue A is positioned within the footprint of the new plant. Because the pole directly conflicts with the building placement, access points, and required construction clearances, FPL must relocate the pole to allow the project to move forward safely and in compliance with utility requirements.
The relocation work provided by FPL delivers several key project outcomes, including:
• Removal of the existing pole from the new plant’s impact zone.
• Installation of a newly positioned utility pole at a location that meets all safety, electrical, and construction clearances.
• Reconfiguration and reconnection of the electrical infrastructure supported by the pole, ensuring uninterrupted service and proper integration with the new plant layout.
• Clearance of the construction footprint, enabling foundation work, equipment installation, and site access to proceed without obstruction.
This relocation is essential to avoid construction delays, maintain project compliance, and ensure that all utilities are safely and properly routed to support the new plant.

description:
At the May 28th meeting, Attorney Smith advised this resolution would be forthcoming to address the legislation adopted to overhaul the building permit fee rules in the State of Florida. The changes signed into law by Governor DeSantis take effect July 1.
A summary of these changes are:
Valuation-Based Fees Capped: Local governments are prohibited from charging inspection fees based on the total cost/valuation of a project. Inspection fees must be restricted to the agency's actual cost to perform and approve the inspection.
Exemption for Smaller Projects: Permits and their associated fees are no longer required for single-family residential projects valued at less than $7,500 (though electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas, and structural work remain exceptions).
Private Provider Fee Reductions: If you use a private provider for commercial plan reviews or inspections, local governments are mandated to reduce your permit fees by specified percentages (50% for full private provider services or 25% for partial).
HOA Permit Bans: The bill prevents local Homeowner Associations (HOAs) from demanding a building permit as a prerequisite for their architectural reviews.
Section 2 of Resolution 2026–54 amends Resolution 2026-28. Adopted April 23, 2026, Resolution 2026-28 reduced the building permit fees collected by 75% (such that the applicants paid for 25% of the Residential/Commercial Permit Fees). The amendment retains a reduction from the adopted fees but replaces the 75% reduction with a 25% reduction (such that the applicants pay for 75% of the Residential/Commercial Permit Fees).
