description:
One update has been included since first reading to provide clarification. Section 4-107 Exemptions from special event requirements. The underlined italic portion of the last sentence is new.
(d) Home-based craft vendors and cottage food vendors who do not hold a LBTR shall be exempt from requirement to provide an LBTR, provided that the vendor presents proof of registration with the Florida Department of Revenue for the collection and remittance of sales tax, along with completing an IM application and paying the IM permit fee.
The City of Flagler Beach applied for and received the 2024 Flagler County Tourism Development Council Capital Project Grant funds to renovate the Pier’s service building and to build a 4,000 square foot promenade which will be used for events. Flagler County and the City entered into a funding agreement, approved by the City Commission in Resolution 2024-72. The grant proposal and funding agreement requires the City to update its Special Events Ordinance in preparation of the new facility, which is expected to bring more special event activities.
The Special Events Ordinance was first adopted to the City of Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances in 2002.
The following proposed Special Events Ordinance was edited and reviewed by staff, including the City Clerk, Deputy City Clerk, the City Attorney, and Police Leadership. The revisions reflect current practices, provide administrative flexibility, streamline requirements, and encourage adherence by staff and applicants.
While this staff report details section-by-section edits, several reoccurring modifications appear throughout the proposed ordinance and are not repeated in each section:
1. Removal of “permit”: Staff does not issue a permit; written approval is granted, usually via email. The ordinance now reflects this practice.
2. Removal of “special event planning meeting”: This change allows staff to adopt internal review processes that can adapt over time. It does not prevent staff from requesting a planning meeting when necessary.
3. Removal of references to positions: Except for the City Manager and Police Chief, references to specific positions were removed or replaced with “and/or designee” to provide flexibility in delegating responsibilities.
4. Site plan sketch: A site plan sketch is now required with the Special Event Application (SEA) and referenced throughout the ordinance.
5. Fee Schedule reference: The ordinance now aligns with the City’s practice of adopting an annual Fee Schedule by resolution.
6. Section sequence: Sec. 4-104 through Sec. 4-107 were moved for the proper sequence of the complete application process.
7. Grammar adjustments: Capitalization and other minor changes.
Sec. 4-102. Section was reorganized eliminate redundancy. The article establishes that all special events require City approval through the Special Event Application (SEA). Part (b) was moved to Sec. 4-110. Alcohol and Beverage Sale and part (c) wording was moved to Sec. 4-105. (b)(4).
Sec. 4-103. Definitions.Applicant(s). The definition was changed to properly reference SEAs.
Certificate of Insurance. Definition was added due to its significance.
City Event. Removal of “sponsor” to prevent confusion.
City Services. Added definition due to significance.
Commercial. Clarified to include the orders of goods and services.
Cottage food vendor. Added to recognize an increase in Itinerant Merchant applications from these vendors. Referenced later in the code under Sec. 4-107.
Fees. References the Fee Schedule adopted by the City Commission through resolution.
Home-based craft vendor. Added to recognize increased home-based craft vendors; referenced in Sec. 4-107.
Special Event. Clarified and unrelated portions relocated.
Classifications of Event: Major, Intermediate, and Minor were adjusted to better reflect the forms of applications that the city receives: city services totaling $2,500 and over, between $2,499 and $500, and below $499, respectively.
Special Event Permit. The definition was removed.
Temporary Structure. The definition includes reference to a set-up time.
Itinerant Merchant (IM). Modified to include orders for goods and services, and redundant wording was removed.
Sec. 4-104. Part (a) provides a timeline for the applicant to submit an SEA based on event classification. City Commission approval requirements for major events was removed to streamline the application process. Reference to payments and fees was moved to Sec. 4-108. Denial of an application and its costs are described in Sec. 4-105(b) and (d). Part (b) clarifies additional documents to include with the SEA, adopting wording from the former part (c).
Sec. 4-105. The section establishes actions that the city shall take within 10 business days of receipt of the SEA, a change from the original five days. For centralization, disapproval reasons found throughout the ordinance was place in part (b). Part (c) offers the applicant an appeal option if an event is disapproved, and (d) removes refund language.
Sec. 4-106. Clarifies applicant and IM responsibility before, during, and after an event, and provides a timeline for payment of IM permit fees. Part (b) was edited to provide a time frame for required documents, part (e) was taken from another part of the code and placed here as it pertains to IMs. Part (f) was originally Sec. 4-122 but was moved to this section.
Sec. 4-107. Parts (a), (b), and (c) were edited for clarity. Part (d) exempts home-based crafters and cottage food vendors from providing an LBTR, responding to the rise in IM permit requests. This change makes events more accessible to these small-scale vendors, who often lack the required documentation.
Sec. 4-108. Edited for clarity, to provide a time frame for payment, and amount needed for a deposit.
Sec. 4-110. Edited for centralization of alcohol provisions. Reference added to Sec. 4-127(b)(4).
Sec. 4-111. Section (a) rewritten for clarity.
Sec. 4-114. Part(a) was edited to remove conflicting verbiage; portable toilet formula was retained.
Sec. 4-115. The formula in part (b) was updated to reflect current sanitation practices. A time frame was added for removal of dumpsters following an event.
Sec. 4-121. Edits made for clarity.
Sec. 4-125. Generalized provisions to provide staff flexibility.
Sec. 4-127. Edits made to (b)(4) b. to properly reference the updated code.

description:
This item passed first reading at the September 25, 2025 meeting. City staff were directed to research and prepare building access regulations that maintain a safe, orderly environment on city-owned, controlled, and leased property. Due to the enforceability of this item, the regulation comes before the Commission as an Ordinance instead of a Resolution.
The Ordinance recognizes the City's authority to create building access regulations based on the property's intended use and its classification that are consistent with decisions of the United States Supreme Court. City buildings will be regulated as nonpublic forums and limited public forums. Staff recommended that a visual guide establishing forums be included in the ordinance, attached as exhibits. In addition to these exhibits, the City Manager shall manage public access to City buildings, and shall employ appropriate measures to implement the proposed ordinance.
The proposed ordinance has been reviewed by the City Clerk, City Manager, and the City Attorney.
title: Ordinance 2025-20. An Ordinance by the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, amending the Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances, Chapter 14, creating Section 14-14, Public Access to City Buildings, providing recognition that certain areas of city buildings require regulation of public access to provide for the security and privacy of public visitors, city employees, city officials, and minimize potential disruptions of the work of city government; classifying certain forum areas within city buildings; authorizing the City Manager to manage public access to City buildings by classifying forum areas and implementing measures to separate forum areas, regulate access and ensure security and privacy, providing for violations for unauthorized access or disruptive behavior within nonpublic and limited public forums; providing the authority to issue trespass warnings; providing for codifications, conflicts, and an effective date. description:

description:
The City acquired the properties upon which the Ocean Palm Golf Course is located in two transactions (2013 and 2022). The City leased the golf course to Flagler Golf Management in 2015, the lease for which was subsequently assigned to Ocean Palms Golf Club LLC. During discussions after the assignment, representatives of Ocean Palms Golf Club LLC expressed interest in purchasing the properties as part of their proposed redevelopment effort. Specifically conditioned by the City Commission as part of any prospective sale was that the properties were to be restricted solely to golf course operations.
City staff obtained three appraisals based upon the restrictive condition set by the City Commission, with all three appraisals similarly indicating a value of approximately $800,000 (all three appraisers cautioned that the restrictive condition constrained their appraisals from considering higher appraisals based upon residential or commercial uses). At its Jul 10 City Commission Regular Meeting, the City Commission authorized the City Manager to sign a non-binding Letter of Intent describing the proposed terms and conditions for the sale of the two golf course properties.
Through counsel, Ocean Palms Golf Club LLC submitted the attached Purchase and Sale Agreement for City Commission consideration. An Intent to Purchase/Lease from TRC (Trinity Restoration and Contracting) was submitted to City staff on Oct 2, 2025 and is included in the agenda package.
Regardless of what decision the City Commission makes regarding the Purchase and Sale Agreement, additional City Commission action will be required (First and Second Readings of a proposed Ordinance at future City Commission meetings) for further consideration. Even if consideration of one of the proposals is desired, the existing lease will remain in place and the properties cannot be sold as part of this meeting.
title: Consider Agreements for the Purchase/Lease of Golf Course Properties.

description:
While looking for a code, it was discovered that Chapter 6, Beaches and Recreation of the Code of Ordinances, prohibits events from lasting longer than one (1) day in parks. The TNT Craft Show has held its two (2) day events (plus an additional 1/2 day of vendor set up on Friday) in Veterans Park three (3) times per year since December 2011. description:
The City of Flagler Beach undertook the Pump Station 11 Emergency Relining Project to address structural deterioration within the pump station’s force main system. The contract was originally awarded to Atlantic Pipe Services in the amount of $29,159.66.
During construction, unforeseen conditions were encountered that required additional labor, materials, and time. These items included:
Additional slip lining footage beyond the original measured scope due to deteriorated pipe sections.
Extra cleaning and debris removal, including heavy grease deposits and root intrusion.
Adjustments to bypass pumping operations to maintain uninterrupted wastewater service.
Sealing of unexpected pipe defects and lateral connections to ensure watertight system integrity.
These additional services increased the purchase order to $39,309.66 under emergency demand. Upon completion of the project, a final Change Order (No. 1) in the amount of $15,306.01 is required to reconcile the full scope of work performed.
title: Resolution 2025-84. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, to approve a Change Order submitted by Atlantic Pipe Solutions for emergency repairs to Pump Station 11 Slip Lining Project in an amount not to exceed $15,306.01; providing for conflict and an effective date.

The City Attorney to review and determine if PARB recommendation aligns with the intent of SB 784.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach has identified the need to resurface and pave designated city streets to improve roadway conditions to ensure public safety and extend the service life of its transportation infrastructure. Using a road assessment software, Public Works staff gathered and uploaded street data to determine the quality of roads throughout the City. Streets in the poorest condition were selected to be improved as part of this project, including:Palm Avenue from Springdale Drive to the end of the Cul-De-Sac
South 26th Street from A1A to Lakeshore Drive
North Flagler From Moody Blvd to North 2nd Street
South Central from 21st Street to 23rd Street
Although the initial quote did not include the repaving of South Central, the City Commission directed staff to include S. Central.
With Request for Qualification (RFQ) 2025-1806, the City Commission, at its June 26, 2025 Regular Meeting approved the list of vetted vendors. The City’s Public Works staff has evaluated the proposed improvements and determined that the project is in the public interest and consistent with the City’s capital improvement goals. Staff have reviewed and vetted the contracts and references of Sparks Concrete, LLC.

Ordinance 2025-14 passed first reading with an amendment at the August 28, 2025, meeting. The amendment was to include the deletion of Section 5-31. City of Flagler Beach Dog Friendly Dining Program. The amendment was included and appears between lines 118 and 225 of the ordinance.
The amendments in this ordinance relate to items that are no longer applicable or amendments were approved that change the process. The following are the amendments and the cause to amend.
Section 6-41. Use Charges (Line 33–41) The fees for rental of the Wickline Center rooms are amended to remove the fee for the single classroom or lobby as these spaces are now or soon will be occupied by staff. The rates for the Senior Center (Great room) are included in Resolution 2025-65 (on this agenda for consideration).
Section 5-6. Requirements for Registration of Animals (line 45–58) The requirement to register and purchase an animal license for pets ended last year at the direction of the City Commission.
Section 5-19. Fees (Line 62–114) This amendment removes the registration fee, replacement tag fee, and the penalty for not registering.
Section 3-19. Permit for Non-Profit Organization; application; approval (Line 122–140). This section refers to the Building Official and should refer to the Planner. A non-profit organization wanting to dispense liquor would apply for a temporary license from the Department of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms. That application requires zoning approval by the local government's Planner.
Section 16-18. Application; fee (Line 149–196) This section pertains to the issuance of door-to-door solicitation permits. The process in how background checks are performed has changed. The checks were previously performed by our Police Department. Legislation regulating how the Police can access information in the Driver & Vehicle Information Database (DAVID) limited information and lengthened the turnaround time to complete the background check. The City now utilizes the same company that performs new hire background screening for these applications. Fingerprints are no longer required, the fee is increased to cover the cost of the background checks, and is also included in Resolution 2025-65 and the responsibility to approve is removed from the police.
Section 16-20. Surety Bond and 16-24. (Line 200–218) This also applies to the issuance of a Door-to-Door Solicitation license. Removing the requirement to provide a surety bond.
Section 19-55. Enforcement (Line 222–228) Removes the requirement for the Clerk to maintain a truck route map.
Section 22-52. Building Permit, fee (line 237–247) Removing an outdated code that required a resident to pay the City Clerk $5.00 for the construction of 100 feet of bulk head.

description:
Ordinance 2025-15 passed first reading at the August 28, 2025, meeting. Resolution 2025-80 is presented to set the qualifying period for the 2026 Municipal Election.
The City Clerk was notified by the Supervisor of Elections Office that the deadline for the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) to mail ballots overseas is January 17, 2026. This conflicts with the City's qualifying period. The Charter requires regular qualifying to begin the day after the first meeting in January and continue for 5 business days, putting the City's qualifying opening on January 9th and ending on the 15th. These dates do not allow enough time for the Election Office to get the ballots printed and postmarked by the 17th. A workaround for this issue is to hold a special meeting on January 5th, which is a Monday, and the regular qualifying will end at 5:00 pm on January 12th. This solution would only apply to the 2026 qualifying period, and would continue to be an issue going forward, as the UOCAVA rule is that overseas ballots for the military have to be mailed 45 days in advance of an election.
The second issue is Section 7.05 (b) of the Charter regarding run-off elections. Our charter states that in the event of a tie, the run-off elections shall be no later than 35 days after the election. This would not meet the UOCAVA rules.
After seeking advice from Attorney Smith, he advised Sections 166.021(4) and 100.3605, Florida Statutes, allow cities to amend their charters by ordinance to change the dates for qualifying and for election of members and provide for the orderly transition of office resulting from such date changes. Therefore, the Commission can adopt language via an ordinance, without having to go to a referendum to align with the compliance deadlines established by Florida Statutes and Florida Election Code Chapter 97-106.
The adoption of this ordinance will resolve the qualifying and run-off scheduling issues and bring compliance.
title: Ordinance 2025-15. An Ordinance by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, amending the City Charter Sections 7.05(b) Runoff and 7.02(a) Qualifying; modifying the runoff election date and qualifying period for the 2026 General Municipal Election and in each subsequent year except for those years that are multiples of four (4) to a period that is in harmony with the Statutory Vote-By-Mail requirements imposed on the Supervisor of Elections; providing for severability; providing for conflicts; providing for codification; and providing an effective date (Second [Final] Reading).

description:
Ordinance 2025-15, amended the Flagler Beach Charter for the qualifying period for Municipal Elections to be compliant with the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA). A requirement of this ordinance is for the City Clerk to present a Resolution setting the qualifying period to the City Commission for approval.
Resolution 2025-80 establishes the 2026 City of Flagler Beach Municipal Election Qualifying Period beginning on December 12, 2025, at 9:00a.m. and continuing for five working days ending at 5:00 p.m. on December 18, 2025. Candidates would be required to pay the 1% State Elections Assessment ($104.43) and 6% of the annual salary ($626.58) a total of $731.01.
Potential Candidates may also qualify via the Petition Process starting at 9:00 a.m. on Tuesday, September 23, 2025. Candidates must first come meet with the City Clerk to complete their DSDE9 Appointment of Campaign Treasurer, provide proof of residency and voter registration before they begin collecting petitions. Then those 45 valid petitions (1% of the registered voters at the close of the deadline to register at the 2024 General Election) must be certified by the Flagler County Supervisor of Elections before the deadline of Noon on November 13, 2025, 28 day prior to the start of regular qualifying per Section 99.095 (3) Florida Statutes.
title: Resolution 2025-80. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, designating the dates of the Qualifying Period for the 2026 Municipal Election; providing for conflict and an effective date.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach applied for and received the 2024 Flagler County Tourism Development Council Capital Project Grant funds to renovate the Pier’s service building and to build a 4,000 square foot promenade which will be used for events. Flagler County and the City entered into a funding agreement, approved by the City Commission in Resolution 2024-72. The grant proposal and funding agreement requires the City to update its Special Events Ordinance in preparation of the new facility, which is expected to bring more special event activities.
The Special Events Ordinance was first adopted to the City of Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances in 2002.
The following proposed Special Events Ordinance was edited and reviewed by staff, including the City Clerk, Deputy City Clerk, the City Attorney, and Police Leadership. The revisions reflect current practices, provide administrative flexibility, streamline requirements, and encourage adherence by staff and applicants.
While this staff report details section-by-section edits, several reoccurring modifications appear throughout the proposed ordinance and are not repeated in each section:
1. Removal of “permit”: Staff does not issue a permit; written approval is granted, usually via email. The ordinance now reflects this practice.
2. Removal of “special event planning meeting”: This change allows staff to adopt internal review processes that can adapt over time. It does not prevent staff from requesting a planning meeting when necessary.
3. Removal of references to positions: Except for the City Manager and Police Chief, references to specific positions were removed or replaced with “and/or designee” to provide flexibility in delegating responsibilities.
4. Site plan sketch: A site plan sketch is now required with the Special Event Application (SEA) and referenced throughout the ordinance.
5. Fee Schedule reference: The ordinance now aligns with the City’s practice of adopting an annual Fee Schedule by resolution.
6. Section sequence: Sec. 4-104 through Sec. 4-107 were moved for the proper sequence of the complete application process.
7. Grammar adjustments: Capitalization and other minor changes.
Sec. 4-102. Section was reorganized eliminate redundancy. The article establishes that all special events require City approval through the Special Event Application (SEA). Part (b) was moved to Sec. 4-110. Alcohol and Beverage Sale and part (c) wording was moved to Sec. 4-105. (b)(4).
Sec. 4-103. Definitions.Applicant(s). The definition was changed to properly reference SEAs.
Certificate of Insurance. Definition was added due to its significance.
City Event. Removal of “sponsor” to prevent confusion.
City Services. Added definition due to significance.
Commercial. Clarified to include the orders of goods and services.
Cottage food vendor. Added to recognize an increase in Itinerant Merchant applications from these vendors. Referenced later in the code under Sec. 4-107.
Fees. References the Fee Schedule adopted by the City Commission through resolution.
Home-based craft vendor. Added to recognize increased home-based craft vendors; referenced in Sec. 4-107.
Special Event. Clarified and unrelated portions relocated.
Classifications of Event: Major, Intermediate, and Minor were adjusted to better reflect the forms of applications that the city receives: city services totaling $2,500 and over, between $2,499 and $500, and below $499, respectively.
Special Event Permit. The definition was removed.
Temporary Structure. The definition includes reference to a set-up time.
Itinerant Merchant (IM). Modified to include orders for goods and services, and redundant wording was removed.
Sec. 4-104. Part (a) provides a timeline for the applicant to submit an SEA based on event classification. City Commission approval requirements for major events was removed to streamline the application process. Reference to payments and fees was moved to Sec. 4-108. Denial of an application and its costs are described in Sec. 4-105(b) and (d). Part (b) clarifies additional documents to include with the SEA, adopting wording from the former part (c).
Sec. 4-105. The section establishes actions that the city shall take within 10 business days of receipt of the SEA, a change from the original five days. For centralization, disapproval reasons found throughout the ordinance was place in part (b). Part (c) offers the applicant an appeal option if an event is disapproved, and (d) removes refund language.
Sec. 4-106. Clarifies applicant and IM responsibility before, during, and after an event, and provides a timeline for payment of IM permit fees. Part (b) was edited to provide a time frame for required documents, part (e) was taken from another part of the code and placed here as it pertains to IMs. Part (f) was originally Sec. 4-122 but was moved to this section.
Sec. 4-107. Parts (a), (b), and (c) were edited for clarity. Part (d) exempts home-based crafters and cottage food vendors from providing an LBTR, responding to the rise in IM permit requests. This change makes events more accessible to these small-scale vendors, who often lack the required documentation.
Sec. 4-108. Edited for clarity, to provide a time frame for payment, and amount needed for a deposit.
Sec. 4-110. Edited for centralization of alcohol provisions. Reference added to Sec. 4-127(b)(4).
Sec. 4-111. Section (a) rewritten for clarity.
Sec. 4-114. Part(a) was edited to remove conflicting verbiage; portable toilet formula was retained.
Sec. 4-115. The formula in part (b) was updated to reflect current sanitation practices. A time frame was added for removal of dumpsters following an event.
Sec. 4-121. Edits made for clarity.
Sec. 4-125. Generalized provisions to provide staff flexibility.
Sec. 4-127. Edits made to (b)(4) b. to properly reference the updated code.

description:
City staff were directed to research and prepare building access regulations that maintain a safe, orderly environment on city-owned, controlled, and leased property. Due to the enforceability of this item, the regulation comes before the Commission as an Ordinance instead of a Resolution.
The Ordinance recognizes the City's authority to create building access regulations based on the property's intended use and its classification that are consistent with decisions of the United States Supreme Court. City buildings will be regulated as nonpublic forums and limited public forums. Staff recommended that a visual guide establishing forums be included in the ordinance, attached as exhibits. In addition to these exhibits, the City Manager shall manage public access to City buildings, and shall employ appropriate measures to implement the proposed ordinance.
The proposed ordinance has been reviewed by the City Clerk, City Manager, and the City Attorney.

description:
The City Commission approved Resolution 2025-43 to temporarily reduce building permit fees at its April 24, 2025, Regular Commission Meeting in response to two audit findings that concluded the current fee structure exceeds the cost-of-service provision per Section 553.80(7)(a).
Resolution 2025-70 extends the temporary reduction of select building permit fees by 50% for the period of October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026. The reduced fees apply to categories including total construction cost permits, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, mobile home, residential pool/spa permits, and specific applications such as demolition, house moving, roofing, siding, windows, temporary construction trailers, and signage. Any fees paid after October 1, 2025, and before the effective date will be partially refunded to reflect the reduction. The reduced fees will sunset on September 30, 2026, unless the City Commission adopts a future resolution extending or amending the fee schedule. This resolution also repeals any conflicting resolutions, specifically Resolution 2025-43, and incorporates standard provisions for conflicts, severability, and effective date.

description: The City of Flagler Beach undertook the South Central Water Main Replacement Project (Project No. 570), per Bid No. FB-24-1021; and awarded the contract to All State Civil Construction, Inc. for the amount of $610,409.00 under Resolution 2025-01. This change order pertains to the 12-inch by 8-inch tapping sleeve, valve and associated equipment rental delay due to unforeseen field conditions encountered at the intersection of South Central Avenue and South 3rd Street. To continue the same level of service, the 12-inch water main connection to the newly placed 8-inch required a 12-inch by 8-inch tapping sleeve and valve.

description:
The City Commission annually determines proposed Legislative Priorities to present to the Legislative Delegation for State funding or policymaking. Previous efforts have sought funding assistance for water system improvements, wastewater system improvements, and flood protection.
Although the Legislative Session does not officially convene until January 13, 2026, it is imperative to determine the City's priorities so that the requests can be appropriately submitted for review and consideration. The Northeast Florida Regional Council and Flagler County compile local requests to present collaboratively to the Legislative Delegation. The Legislative Delegation meeting has been scheduled for 3:00 PM, September 19, at the Flagler County General Services Building (Commission Chambers).
The first priority is based upon the future need for the City to comply with the regulations for wastewater treatment discharge. The City's Re-Use Plan (2024) indicates the design and construction of a Reverse Osmosis Treatment System and Transfer Pump Station to begin the compliance transition. The request is for $1,500,000 (supplemented by $1,500,000 of City funds) for the project.
The second priority is to support the City's resiliency effort to protect critical City facilities located on S. Flagler Avenue. An earlier grant funded the design of a berm to be placed west of the facilities. The City has pursued additional grant funding for the construction of the berm, but has been unsuccessful to date in obtaining that funding. The request is for $1,500,000 (supplmented by $1,500,000 of City funds) for the project.
title: Resolution 2025-77. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, adopting priority projects to present to the City’s Legislative Delegation requesting supplemental state funding; providing for conflict and an effective date.

description:
Land Use Data
Applicant: Joseph Pozzuoli, Architect
Owner: Gaspar Family Holdings
Property Address: 907 N Ocean Shore Blvd., Flagler Beach, FL
Parcel ID: 01-12-31-1100-00050-0050 .14 of an acre
Zoning: Tourist Commercial
Overlay: Downtown Mixed-Use Overlay
FLUM: Commercial
Background
February 2025, applicant for the owner attended Technical Review Committee (TRC) to gather technical feedback on a proposed two-story, mixed-use building with approximately 2513 SQ.FT. per floor. The first floor proposes two (2) retail spaces and a 2-car garage with exterior stairs that lead to a three (3) bedroom, two (2) bath dwelling unit.
Variance Request
Design Guidelines Section 02.04.02 (2) and (5)
The applicant is requesting a variance from the Land Development Code, Article II, Section 2.04.02. Design Guidelines, Location (2) and (5).(2) - Individual ingress and egress drives extending across the public sidewalks and curbs connecting the off-street parking spaces to the public street areas shall not exceed a maximum of twelve (12') feet for a one-way drive and eighteen (18') feet for a two-way drive.
Applicant requests relief from the land development code minimum standards for a two-way drive requiring eighteen feet (18’) for a two-way drive for commercial use to a twelve-foot (12’) lane for a two-way commercial use drive. (5) - Joint common access drives and shared parking provisions are encouraged for two (2) or more contiguous interior lots owned exclusively or under separate ownership to enhance two-way access, thereby decreasing access width from fifteen (15') feet to twelve (12') feet for each lot.
The applicant requests relief from the land development code minimum standards for a joint common access drive on a contiguous interior commercial lot, decreasing the land development code minimum standards for two-way access from twelve feet (12’) on each lot to six feet (6’) on each lot.
Planning and Architectural Review Board Section 8.05.13
The Planning and Architectural Review Board (PARB) may recommend granting variances only upon finding that the request meets the six standards set forth in Appendix A, Land Development Regulations, Section 8.05.13.
In advocating any variance, the Planning and Architectural Review Board may prescribe appropriate conditions and safeguards in conformity with this ordinance. Violation of such conditions and safeguards, when made a part of the terms under which the variance is advocated, shall be deemed a violation of this ordinance.
The Planning and Architectural Review Board may prescribe a reasonable time limit within which the action for which the variance is required shall be begun or completed or both. Under no circumstances except as permitted above shall the Planning and Architectural Review Board advocate a variance to permit use not generally or by special exception permitted in the zoning district involved or any use expressly or by implication prohibited by the terms of this ordinance in the zoning district.
No nonconforming use of neighboring lands, structures or buildings in the same zoning district, and no permitted use of lands, structures or buildings in other zoning districts shall be considered grounds for the advocation of a variance.
Staff Analysis Appropriate Conditions and Safeguards Section 8.05.13
1. That special conditions and circumstances exist which are peculiar to the land, structure or building involved and which are not applicable to other structures or buildings in the same zoning district. a. No special conditions or circumstances exist which are peculiar to the land which are not applicable to other commercial buildings in the same zoning district. Other commercial properties on State Route (S. R.) A1A are required to meet the standards, including those lots platted at 50’ along S. Ocean Shore/A1A.
b. A1A is a state road and FDOT requirements for driveways are more stringent than the City’s land development code. FDOT requires commercial properties to have two-way access and be a minimum of twenty-four feet (24’).
2. That the special conditions and circumstances do not result from the actions of the applicant.a. The circumstances are the result of the actions of the applicant/owner due to the building size of the proposed project. The size of the project does not accommodate a two-way drive width.
b. The Land Development Code encourages and makes concessions for by joint access drives by decreasing the two-way access width from fifteen-feet (15’) to twelve-feet (12’) on each lot.
3. That granting the variance requested will not confer on the applicant any special privilege that is denied by this ordinance to other lands, buildings or structures in the same zoning district.a. The granting of this variance confers special privileges which are denied to other commercial property in the same zoning district.
4. That literal interpretation of the provisions of this ordinance would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in the same zoning district under the terms of this ordinance and would work unnecessary and undue hardship on the applicant. a. The granting of variance does not deprive the applicant of rights enjoyed by other properties in the same zoning district.
5. That the variance granted is the minimum variance that will make possible the reasonable use of the land, building or structure,a. The minimal granting of a variance will not make possible the reasonable use of the land as a smaller commercial structure and/or mixed-use building can be built to accommodate a two-way joint commercial drive.
6. That the grant of the variance will be in harmony with the general intent and purpose of this ordinance, and that such a variance will not be injurious to the area involved or otherwise detrimental to the public welfare.a. The project proposes a joint/shared drive contiguous with the commercial property to the north with each commercial lot providing 6’ drive easement to be utilized as a two-way drive. The commercial property to the north is listed on the property appraiser’s site as a restaurant/café use. Both commercial properties utilizing a one-way twelve-foot (12’) drive for ingress/egress onto A1A, Ocean Shore Blvd is potentially injurious or otherwise detrimental to the public.
PARB Meeting 08/05/2025
On August 05, 2025, the Planning & Architecturial Board recommended that the City Commission approve with conditions the variance request in a vote of five to one. The following are draft minutes from the meeting.
Application PVAR25-0002: Variance – Applicant is requesting a variance from the Land Development Code, Article II, Section 2.04.02. Design Guidelines, Location (2) and (5). Applicant requests relief from the land development code minimum standards for a two-way drive requiring eighteen feet (18’) for a two-way drive for commercial use to a twelve-foot (12’) lane for a two-way commercial use drive. Parcel ID No.: 01-12-31-1100-00050-0050; FLUM: Commercial; Zoning District: Tourist Commercial; Owner: Gaspar Family Holding Three LLC, 908 N Central Avenue, Flagler Beach, FL 32136; Applicant: Gaspar Family Holding Three LLC, 908 N Central Avenue, Flagler Beach, FL. 32136; Representative: Joseph Pozzuoli Architect, P.A., 314 Moody Boulevard, Flagler Beach, FL 32136.
City Attorney, Drew Smith, presented the item. The City Planner, Lupita McClenning, was not present, but the City Planner's staff findings were included in the agenda packet. City Engineer, Bill Freeman, was present to answer technical questions. Attorney Smith directed the Board to page 55 of the agenda packet which outlines the six criteria required and the relevant staff findings. Attorney Smith outlined the requirements needed for a recommendation to the City Commission to approve the request. Representatives of the applicant, Joseph Pozzuoli and Deborah Bird, were present and spoke before the Board. Mr. Pozzuoli outlined his response to the six requirements needed for the variance to be approved. Mr. Pozzuoli’s comments included the conditions related to the existing development surrounding the subject property created a hardship for the applicant to include a shared driveway, a building to the south and the size of the lot (applicant provided a printout from the Land Development Code section 2.02.04 which is attached to the minutes). Board discussion ensued and comments included the square footage of the proposed project, changing the building footprint, FDOT requirements, Ocean Shore Boulevard regulations in the Land Development Code, shared driveway challenges, existing development with similar challenges, travel trips, width of the city streets, minimum width for a two-way driveway, frontage guidelines, creating a handicap parallel parking space in front of the building, a possible state handicap parking variance through the Florida Building Code, mixed-use district parking regulations, challenges with existing non-conforming lot, existing city streets, and concerns with future development. Discussion ensued with Attorney Smith to amend the variance request. Paul Mykytka expressed his concerns and would like to see a wider driveway. Barbara Revels made a motion to recommend approval of item 7b. with the condition that the applicant remove the handicap space in the back of the building and place it in the front of the building, providing for a sixteen (16') foot-wide driveway. Attorney Smith expressed concern to relocating the parking space as part of the motion and whether moving the parking space is permitted. Attorney Smith advised the motion should include only the recommendation for approval with the condition of the applicant meeting a sixteen (16') foot-wide driveway. Barabara Revels amended her motion to recommend approval with the condition of requiring a sixteen (16') foot-wide driveway. Paul Mykytka inquired with the City Engineer if the sixteen (16') foot-wide driveway was sufficient. The City Engineer, Bill Freeman, stated the sixteen feet (16') would be tight, but sufficient. Scott Chappuis seconded the motion. Attorney Smith stated for the record there was no public present, and no public comment was received.
Roll Call: Boudie Estberg, Nay; Lisa Smith: Yea; Scott Chappuis, Yea; Barbara Revels, Yea; Paul Mykytka, Yea; Chair Suzie Johnston, Yea. Motion passed five (5) to one (1).

description:
Project OverviewThe applicant proposes to develop small cottages with access from Leslie Street and exiting on Joyce Street. Leslie and Joyce Streets have a 40-foot right-of-way (ROW). Leslie Street is currently paved and has utilities within the ROW.

description:
The Flagler Beach Wastewater Treatment Plant was constructed in 1987. The plant has two clarifiers (designated as the North and the South Clarifier) which contribute to the initial process of wastewater treatment, separating solid material from liquid. Only one clarifier is operational at this time: the North Clarifier's underground piping has a blockage, which renders the clarifier non-functional. Despite several internal efforts, staff could not determine the actual location (even with use of a camera) or alleviate the blockage.
Using the terms of a previously procured contract from the City of Orlando ("piggyback"), U.S. Submergent Technologies will insert a high-pressure jetting system to break up and remove the blockage in order to have a fully functional clarifier.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) was created nearly twenty-five years ago to improve the economic and aesthetic conditions of the area (which generally encompasses the downtown area). The City subsequently approved a Downtown Master Plan, providing direction and goals for the CRA (for which the City Commission was appointed to serve as the CRA Executive Board). The City Commission created an Economic Development Task Force in 2009 to further economic development efforts. Minor revisions (primarily related to membership) were made to the Economic Development Task Force over the course of succeeding years, but the Task Force was voluntarily disbanded by its members in March 2023.
City staff strongly believes that CRA success depends on enhanced coordination between the City and CRA businesses. Though City efforts have focused on improving the economic conditions of the community, the City has had minimal direct interaction with area businesses (and vice versa). Creating a Community Redevelopment Area Advisory Board (CRAAB) will provide an opportunity for the City and downtown businesses to engage in a collaborative effort to support area businesses.
The proposed Resolution provides a two-year cycle to review the effectiveness of the CRAAB by the City Commission.

description:
The amendments in this ordinance relate to items that are no longer applicable or amendments were approved that change the process. The following are the amendments and the cause to amend.
Section 6-41 Use Charges (Line 33–41) The fees for rental of the Wickline Center rooms are amended to remove the fee for the single classroom or lobby as these spaces are now or soon will be occupied by staff. The rates for the Senior Center (Great room) are included in Resolution 2025-65 (on this agenda for consideration).
Section 5-6 Requirements for Registration of Animals (line 45–58) The requirement to register and purchase an animal license for pets ended last year at the direction of the City Commission.
Section 5-19 Fees (Line 62–114) This amendment removes the registration fee, replacement tag fee, and the penalty for not registering.
Section 3-19 Permit for Non-Profit Organization; application; approval (Line 122–140). This section refers to the Building Official and should refer to the Planner. A non-profit organization wanting to dispense liquor would apply for a temporary license from the Department of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms. That application requires zoning approval by the local government's Planner.
Section 16-18. Application; fee (Line 149–196) This section pertains to the issuance of door-to-door solicitation permits. The process in how background checks are performed has changed. The checks were previously performed by our Police Department. Legislation regulating how the Police can access information in the Driver & Vehicle Information Database (DAVID) limited information and lengthened the turnaround time to complete the background check. The City now utilizes the same company who performs new hire background screening for these applications. Fingerprints are no longer required, the fee is increased to cover the cost of the background checks, and is also included in Resolution 2025-65 and the responsibility to approve is removed from the police.
Section 16-20 Surety Bond and 16-24 (Line 200–218) This also applies to the issuance of a Door-to-Door Solicitation license. Removing the requirement to provide a surety bond.
Section19-55 Enforcement (Line 222–228) Removes the requirement for the Clerk to maintain a truck route map.
Section 22-52 Building Permit, fee (line 237–247) Removing old code that required a resident to pay the City Clerk $5.00 for the construction of 100 feet of bulk head.

description:
The City Clerk was notified by the Supervisor of Elections Office that the deadline for the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) to mail ballots overseas is January 17, 2026. This conflicts with the City's qualifying period. The Charter requires regular qualifying to begin the day after the first meeting in January and continue for 5 business days, putting the City's qualifying opening on January 9th and ending on the 15th. These dates do not allow enough time for the Election Office to get the ballots printed and postmarked by the 17th. A workaround for this issue is to hold a special meeting on January 5th, which is a Monday, and the regular qualifying will end at 5:00 pm on January 12th. This solution would only apply to the 2026 qualifying period, and would continue to be an issue going forward, as the UOCAVA rule is that overseas ballots for the military have to be mailed 45 days in advance of an election.
The second issue is Section 7.05 (b) of the Charter regarding run-off elections. Our charter says In the event of a tie, the run-off elections shall be no later than 35 days after the election. This would not meet the UOCAVA rules.
After seeking advice from Attorney Smith, he advised Sections 166.021(4) and 100.3605, Florida Statutes, allow cities to amend their charters by ordinance to change the dates for qualifying and for election of members and provide for the orderly transition of office resulting from such date changes. Therefore, the Commission can adopt language via an ordinance, without having to go to a referendum to align with the compliance deadlines established by Florida Statutes and Florida Election Code Chapter 97-106.
The adoption of this ordinance will resolve the qualifying and run-off scheduling issues and bring compliance.
title: Ordinance 2025-15. An Ordinance by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, amending the City Charter Sections 7.05(b) Runoff and 7.02(a) Qualifying; modifying the runoff election date and qualifying period for the 2026 General Municipal Election and in each subsequent year except for those years that are multiples of four (4) to a period that is in harmony with the Statutory Vote-By-Mail requirements imposed on the Supervisor of Elections; providing for severability; providing for conflicts; providing for codification; and providing an effective date (First Reading).

description:
We have the opportunity to change our election schedule to follow the County's schedule. Palm Coast changed to follow the County's election cycle a few years ago. Flagler Beach currently foots the bill for the entire election when Bunnell or Beverly Beach have no candidates on the ballot in a presidential preference election year. With laws requiring English and Spanish sample ballots to be mailed and the early voting drop boxes required to be manned, the costs of Flagler Beach elections have increased. Additionally, the request for early voting ballots has increased, and the City is billed for the mailing costs. In this scenario, the election cost is close to $17,000 each year (a potential $68k cost savings over 4 years). I have attached the Palm Coast Ordinance with its charter amendments to make the change.
The change would result in four-year terms for elected officials. Terms will shorten and lengthen during the transition period.
A change to the County cycle is a good option because cost savings are notable. Instead of budgeting $14,000 to $18,000 per year, no cost would be anticipated unless the City had Charter amendments requiring another ballot page. Those costs would be minimal and attributed to additional printing and mailing costs. Additional mailings would be for the registered voters that reside in Ocean Palm South - the portion of the City that is physically located in Volusia County. Another benefit for your constituents is, by aligning with the County election schedule, the City would be able to participate in early voting. Currently, the City does not participate in early voting due to its additional costs.
This item would be a referendum ballot item, and requires the Commission to adopt an ordinance and submit it before the 2026 Election Regular Qualifying closes to be included on the March 3, 2026, Municipal Election ballot.

description:
The employee health, dental and life insurance coverages are due for renewal 10/1/2025. The City currently utilizes Florida Health Care for two health plan options and Florida Blue for one health plan option, Guardian for dental coverage, and Florida Blue Cross Blue Shield for life insurance.
Medical: Through the City’s employee benefit consultant, Brown and Brown, Florida Health Care proposed a renewal at a 13% increase. A market analysis was conducted and proposals were obtained from Florida Health Care, Florida Blue, United Healthcare, Curative, and Cigna with the City selecting United Healthcare as the most competitive provider of healthcare for its full-time employees. United Healthcare proposed a 21.2% premium decrease with a comparative plan.
Dental: The City currently utilizes Guardian as our dental coverage provider. Dental insurance is primarily an employee-paid benefit with a small City contribution. Brown and Brown conducted a market analysis of employee dental insurance and received proposals from Guardian, Humana, United Healthcare and Sun Life. Guardian proposed a 15% premium increase. The other providers’ proposals ranged from a 6% to a 41% increase; however, changes in the provider network would cause more disruption than benefit.
Life: The City currently utilizes Florida Blue Cross Blue Shield as our life insurance provider for all full-time employees. Brown and Brown conducted a market analysis for life insurance and received proposals from Blue Cross Blue Shield, Humana, United Healthcare and Sun Life with proposals ranging from 0% to 68% increases. Florida Blue Cross Blue Shield proposed a 0% increase while maintaining the current benefit program.
Hospital GAP Plan: Staff recommends continuing the American Fidelity Employer Paid Gap Insurance to offset out-of-pocket costs for employees enrolled in our group healthcare plans. There was no increase in cost from last year.

description:
Staff was contacted with an inquiry if the City would consider reducing a code enforcement judgment. The property has been before the Special Magistrate several times. The fines as of Thursday, July 24th have accumulated to the amount of $317,350 and continue to increase by $350.00 each day for two outstanding violations. The respondent resides in California. Staff had been communicating with the respondent via telephone and email. Staff had offered the respondent an opportunity to participate in the hearing via the telephone and attempted to contact them again at the start of the hearing. Below and attached are the findings associated with the case. At this point, the staff seeks direction. Does the Commission wish to reduce the fee if the respondent donates the house to a not-for-profit who plans to demolish the building and sell the property? Or does the Commission wish for Staff to proceed with the foreclosure, demolish the building,and investigate if the property can be used for a stormwater basin, a detention area, or sell the property?
This matter was last heard on the 22nd day of January, 2025, before the Code Enforcement Special Magistrate after due notice to the Respondents and public hearing. The Special Magistrate received evidence, heard testimony and being otherwise duly advised on the premises, made the following Findings of Facts and Ordered.1. The subject property of the code enforcement action is located at 1336 S. Flagler Avenue, Flagler Beach, Florida 32136 and has Tax Parcel ID 18-12-32-2750- 00181-0090.
2. On January 28, 2023, the undersigned entered an order finding the Respondent in violation of Chapter 13 of the City of Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances. Specifically, the undersigned found that both the dilapidated condition of the structure, and the overgrown condition of the lawn caused the Subject Property to be in violation of the requirements of the Code and allowed Respondents a reasonable time within which to cure each condition constituting a violation.
3. On May 26, 2023, the undersigned found that the Respondents had not cured the violations and ordered the imposition of fines.
4. Said Finding of Noncompliance and Imposition of Fine was recorded in the Official Records of Flagler County, Florida, on May 31, 2023, on OR Book 2784, Page 1653.
5. The undersigned noted that at each noticed hearing, Respondents emailed the City to acknowledge receipt of the applicable notices, refused to participate in the statutory hearing process, questioned the authority of the City and of the Magistrate, and threatened legal action.
6. As of January 22, 2025, the Respondents had still not cured the violations that are the subject of the action.
7. The City has established by competent substantial evidence that the prerequisites to commence foreclosure have been met, and the undersigned finds it appropriate to grant permission to foreclose.
Based on the foregoing, it was ordered pursuant to Section 162.09(3), that the City is hereby authorized to institute an action to Foreclose the lien created by the Order Finding Noncompliance and Imposition of Fines.
Ordered on the 30th day of January 2025.
title: Consider a Code Enforcement fine reduction to $10,000 for 1336 S. Flagler Avenue.

description:
For nearly two years, several residents have served on a Parks Ad-Hoc Committee, mainly to shepherd the development of the Wickline Park playground (funded in part by a State grant). The City Commission has approved the Preliminary Site Plan for the playground and staff is preparing documents to solicit contractor interest to build the playground.
With the City Commission's and community's interest in City parks, it is an opportune point to transition to a more formal Parks Committee to consider future park planning and development throughout the City. The formation of the proposed Parks Committee is described in Resolution 2025-61. The appointments to the Parks Committee are intended to follow a similar process to that utilized for the Planning and Architectural Review Board: solicit applications from interested residents and present those applications to the City Commission for consideration and appointment.
Once appointed, the principal task for the Committee will be to prepare a plan for renovations to Veterans Park which would then be submitted to the City for consideration. Funding for renovations would be provided through General Fund or Community Redevelopment Area appropriations and/or additional grants/donations.

description:
The City of Flagler Beach currently utilizes an on-premises accounting system that has become outdated and insufficient to meet the City's growing operational and reporting needs. In response, the Finance Department, in coordination with the City Manager’s Office, evaluated modern cloud-based financial platforms to improve efficiency, security, and integration with other City systems.
Following this evaluation, the Finance Department has recommended BS&A Software as the preferred cloud-based accounting solution. This platform offers enhanced capabilities such as real-time access, scalability, automatic updates, and improved disaster recovery.
The proposed transition is expected to streamline financial operations, enhance reporting accuracy, and reduce long-term IT infrastructure and maintenance costs. The total cost for implementation is estimated at $30,000 and has been reviewed and allocated in the FY24-25 budget through realized audit savings.
This resolution seeks approval for the City Manager to enter into a contract with BS&A for implementation of the new system and authorization to allocate the necessary funds from the General Fund and Enterprise funds.
title: Resolution 2025-53. A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach Authorizing the Transition to Cloud-Based Accounting System and Approval of Related Expenditures, Providing for Conflict and an Effective Date.

description:
Applicant: Compass Hotel Flagler Beach, 111 S. Daytona Avenue, Flagler Beach, Florida 32136. The subject property is zoned General Commercial G.C. The applicant is seeking approval of an Annual Outdoor Entertainment Permit to allow amplified and non-amplified events consisting of music, spoken word and/or other forms of entertainment. Letters were mailed to the surrounding properties. The City was not in receipt of any comments negative or positive.
The applicant indicated they are seeking an annual outdoor entertainment permit to allow ambient music to be heard from exterior speakers in the area of the pool, the covered restaurant area, the commercial shop entrances, and lobby entrance. The applicant indicated they would like to have recorded and live entertainment at the rooftop bar. The type of entertainment is known as "plug and play", generally a one-person, possibly two-person entertainment with a stringed instrument.
At the Planning Board review on June 3rd, Attorney Bayer advised that there would not be rowdy or loud, overbearing entertainment acts as they are not permitted by the Compass and Margaritaville brand/franchise.
The Planning Board recommended approval of the annual permit. Motion by Joann Soman to recommend approval of the Outdoor Entertainment license. Lisa Smith seconded the motion. The option carried unanimously, after a roll call vote.
Section 4-167, Review of Permit Application states that the City Commission, after receiving a recommendation from the Planning and Architectural Review Board (PARB), shall approve, approve with conditions, or deny a permit for outdoor entertainment activity based on any of the following grounds:
(1) The activity would present an adverse impact on the health, safety or welfare of the applicant, participants, public employees or members of the public and/or fail to protect the city's environment.
(2) The activity would unreasonably inconvenience the general public.
(3) The proposed activity is prohibited by or inconsistent with the Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances or the Flagler Beach Comprehensive Plan.
(4) The applicant cannot meet, or is unwilling to meet, all the requirements of this article.
(5) The activity is proposed for a site that does not have adequate parking to accommodate the activity.
(6) The activity is proposed for a site that is inherently hazardous to the participants or the public.
(7) The event would have an adverse effect, and would unreasonably infringe upon, the rights of property owners within two hundred (200) feet of the property line of the subject property.
(8) The event would conflict with another proximate event or interfere with construction or maintenance work.
(9) The information furnished in the application is not materially complete and accurate.
(10) The applicant has violated a provision, restriction or condition of this article or an outdoor entertainment activity permit issued to the applicant within the past and has not presented competent substantial evidence that measures to prevent future violations will be implemented at the property.
(11) The requirements identified by the city staff to ensure public health, safety and welfare have not been met.
(12) The comments and/or recommendations of the planning and architectural review board have not been addressed.
(13) The proposed event or activity is prohibited by federal, state, or local regulations.
(14) Other issues in the public’s interest as identified by the city commission.
(a) In deciding to approve a permit the city commission may limit the type and number of temporary structures and the duration of the activity, including the hours and the number of days of the activity conducted to minimize any adverse impact caused by the activity.
title: Application OE-25-06-01 Request for an Annual Outdoor Entertainment Permit - Compass Hotel 111 S. Daytona Avenue - Applicant - Syra Bhoola - Represented by Attorney Dennis K. Bayer.

description:
City staff are requesting approval by the City Commission to develop and submit a grant proposals:
History: The City was awarded 4486-016-R, City Project #230, a Florida Department of Emergency Management (FDEM) grant from the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) in the amount of $105,000. The grant was approved by the City Commission on December 8, 2022. The grant comes from a Hurricane Mathew disaster fund and requires a 10% local match (see the attached scope of work). The funding covered Phase 1, Design, only. Phase 2, Bidding and Construction, would be awarded pending a Benefit-Cost Analysis (BCA) ratio greater than 1.0. BCAs are typically finalized once the design phase is completed, and a final cost estimate is submitted. If the BCA, which takes several months to complete, is less than 1.0, the project will not be awarded additional funds through HMGP and will not move into Phase 2, Bidding and Construction. The City would have a set of plans which it cannot build.
In 2022, when a grant opportunity arose from the State’s Resilient Florida Grant Program, another FDEM program, staff, with Commission approval, submitted an application to Resilient Florida, as an alternative funding source, or “Plan B”, to cover the construction portion of the project. At the time of submission, Flagler Beach qualified as a Disadvantaged Community, due to its low Mean High Income (MHI), which is determined using Census data, and as a result, the grant would not require a local match.
However, sometime during the FDEM review period, which lasted well into 2023, the latest Census data were released and demonstrated a much higher MHI for Flagler Beach, disqualifying the City's grant application. No recourse was offered, other than resubmitting an application once the Florida Resilient portal reopens.
This request: City staff requests permission from the City Commission to submit an application to the Resilient Florida Grant Program. The program's portal will be open from July 1 – September 1, 2025. The State grant does not require a BCA. The application will request funding for Phase 2, Bidding and Construction of City Project #230. The project will provide flood protection for the four City buildings (Police, Fire, Public Works and Maintenance shops) on South Flagler Avenue (SR100 to S. 7th Street). The project includes regrading of South Flagler Avenue, construction of Miami curbs, storm drain infrastructure, new driveways, and other upgrades to the site. The cost of the construction is estimated to be $3,000,000 with the cost share 50% state/50% local.
\
title: Resolution 2025-48. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, authorizing City Staff to complete and submit a grant application under the Resilient Florida Grant Program; providing for conflict and an effective date.

description:
History: In early 2023, the City received funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA). A portion of this funding was allocated to upgrade four sanitary sewer lift stations. The scope included complete rebuilding and design documentation was done by CPH as City Project #271. When the design documents and final cost estimates were presented to the City Commission, the Commission implemented only one of the four lift stations. Pump Station PS-1, located at 3570 South Central Avenue, was approved by the City Commission at the February 8, 2024, meeting, was bid on, and constructed for $293,000.
This request: The remaining three lift stations are the subject of this Resilient Florida Grant proposal: LS-01 (246 Ocean Palm Drive), PS-05 (South Flagler Avenue & South 3d Street), and PS-08 (Moody Lane at Lantana Avenue). The project is “shovel-ready” with the contract documents ready for bidding. The scope of work includes a complete reconstruction of the stations, repainting, relining, and new internal and external parts and materials consistent with the City’s standard detail for lift stations.
title: Resolution 2025-50. A Resolution by the City Commission of the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, authorizing City Staff to submit a grant application to the Resilient Florida Grant Program for the upgrading of three(3) lift Stations; providing for conflict and an effective date.

description:
On January 31, 2007, the City entered into a Settlement Agreement with Flagler County, the City of Palm Coast, and the Gardens at Hammock Beach Property Owners Association (the “Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement resolved disputes between the parties related to provision of water and sewer services and the project then known as “The Gardens” and now known as “Veranda Bay” was included in the City’s service area. As part of the settlement agreement, the Gardens at Hammock Beach Property Owners Association agreed to transfer certain water and sewer infrastructure to the City upon completion. The successor in interest to Gardens at Hammock Beach Property Owners Association is Gardens at Hammock Beach Community Development District (the “CDD”).
This infrastructure discussed herein is related to that portion of the development already approved by Flagler County and under construction and this acceptance has no relationship to the annexation and development discussions with Veranda Bay.
City staff has reviewed the infrastructure being dedicated to the City and has no concerns regarding its acceptance.
The City Commission is requested to approve acceptance of the Bill of Sale attached hereto as the Exhibits and authorize the Mayor to sign the formal acceptance of same. To reiterate, this acceptance is unrelated to annexation and deals with actual pipes in the ground . Since the pipes are personal property, a bill of sale is utilized rather than a deed. The exhibit will be updated with the OR and page numbers from the recording, and the improvement exhibits will be distributed when received.
title: Resolution 2025-47. A Resolution by the City of Flagler Beach, Florida, accepting the dedication of infrastructure from Gardens at Hammock Beach Community Development District; Veranda Bay Phase 1 through 3 as depicted in the exhibits of the Bill of Sale attached hereto; providing for conflict and effective date.
